68704866-779d-59e5-904f-bed3592a5836.text:
Private Cloud Administrator
The Private Cloud Administrator (PCA) is responsible for building and managing the underlying infrastructure and platform services within the private cloud environment. The PCA operates at the platform level, with visibility and administrative control over the compute, network, storage, and bare-metal resources that form the foundation of the cloud service.

The PCA's responsibilities include defining and onboarding infrastructure resources, configuring the supporting resource profiles and network and storage services, monitoring platform resources, and preparing resources for downstream use. Resources created or onboarded by the PCA are subsequently governed by the Multi-Cloud Administrator before being made available for consumption through the Cloud Tenant Portal.

This section describes the functions available to the PCA and follows the structure of the Paragon navigation interface.

766c1281-09a6-5695-9318-e6afbbbd8813.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Dashboard
The Dashboard is the default page displayed when a Private Cloud Administrator logs in to Paragon. It provides the PCA with an overview of the infrastructure and resources within their administrative scope, including key resource counts, operational states, and recent platform activity.

Resource Summary
The upper section of the Dashboard provides a summary of the resources managed through the platform. Resource counts are displayed for Regions and Zones, while Virtual Machines, Servers, and Elastic IP Pools include additional breakdowns showing their current states or types.

The Transaction Logs page includes a Search field for locating transactions and Start Date & Time and End Date & Time filters for restricting the displayed records to a specific period.

caa7cc64-d7ab-508d-85c4-9449b0d304fd.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute
The Compute section provides the Private Cloud Administrator with visibility into the virtualized compute resources and supporting configurations available within Paragon.

c8f3449c-b393-5621-92de-b677b70f1463.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes
Nodes provide virtualized compute resources that can be provisioned across the providers, regions, and zones available within the platform. In Paragon, the term Node refers to these virtualized compute resources.

For the PCA, the Compute Nodes page provides a view of the nodes provisioned within their administrative scope. The PCA can review node information but does not perform lifecycle or management operations on the nodes from this interface.

97deb1ef-13e1-526c-ba90-f961cd59c0f3.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Compute Nodes
The Compute Nodes page provides a searchable list of nodes and their current configuration and status. The Search field can be used to locate specific nodes, while the Show Deleted option can be enabled to include deleted nodes in the displayed records.

The table displays the following information:
97deb1ef-13e1-526c-ba90-f961cd59c0f3.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Compute Nodes

55292d06-f4da-5c24-b282-b28a0c5bc963.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Additional Node Information
The PCA can view additional information for a node but cannot perform management actions such as starting, stopping, editing, or deleting it.

There are two ways to access the detailed information for a node.

The node Hostname can be selected directly from the Compute Nodes table to open the detailed node view.

Alternatively:

1. Select the checkbox beside the required node.
2. Open the Action menu.
3. Select View More.

Both methods open the detailed view for the selected node, where the PCA can review additional information about the node and its configuration.
55292d06-f4da-5c24-b282-b28a0c5bc963.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Additional Node Information

b58fe413-b641-5a5b-9728-0cbe22aee63d.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes

The Private Cloud Administrator is responsible for creating Node Sizes and defining the compute resources associated with each profile. Newly created Node Sizes are Disabled by default and must subsequently be activated by the Multi-Cloud Administrator before they become available to Cloud Tenant Portal users.

Viewing Node Sizes
The Node Sizes page provides a searchable list of the compute profiles configured in Paragon. The Search field can be used to locate a specific Node Size.

The table displays the following information:
b58fe413-b641-5a5b-9728-0cbe22aee63d.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p012_1.png

a1736266-36fe-53f0-8602-9e3bd2b89464.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Creating a Node Size

8bc8a0d2-d86d-5a47-817e-453b77988b80.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Editing a Node Size
After a Node Size has been created, the PCA can modify its Name. The remaining Node Size configuration cannot be changed through the Edit function.

To edit a Node Size:

1. Select the checkbox beside the required Node Size.
2. Open the Action menu.
3. Select Edit.
4. Update the Node Size name.
5. Submit the change to save the updated name.

Changes to the CPU, memory, GPU configuration, provider, region, or associated zones require a new Node Size to be created.
8bc8a0d2-d86d-5a47-817e-453b77988b80.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Editing a Node Size
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p015_1.png

6aa14a60-0747-5b0f-a323-35afa49bdef4.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images
OS Images are predefined operating system templates used when provisioning virtualized compute nodes. They provide a standardized operating system configuration that can be associated with specific providers, regions, and zones within the platform.

The Private Cloud Administrator is responsible for creating OS Images and defining their underlying configuration. Newly created OS Images are Disabled by default and must be activated by the Multi-Cloud Administrator before they become available to Cloud Tenant Portal users.

Viewing OS Images
The OS Images page provides a searchable list of the operating system images configured in Paragon. The Search field can be used to locate a specific image.

The table displays the following information:
6aa14a60-0747-5b0f-a323-35afa49bdef4.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p016_1.png

c4611692-f0a4-5690-87be-e9887d0b0f58.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Images
The table displays the following information:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the OS Image. |
| Type | Operating system type, such as Linux or Windows. |
| Distribution | Operating system distribution associated with the image, such as Ubuntu or Windows. |
| Root Volume Size | Root volume capacity defined for the image. |
| Template ID | Identifier of the underlying image template used for provisioning. |
| Service Provider Code | Code identifying the service provider associated with the image. |
| Status | Current status of the OS Image, such as Active or Disabled. |
c4611692-f0a4-5690-87be-e9887d0b0f58.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Images

98b40764-b7e8-5552-90d3-063974494058.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Creating an OS Image
Note: The Root Volume Size defined for an OS Image determines the root disk capacity presented to Compute Nodes created using that image.

The root disk size is therefore part of the OS Image definition and is not independently selected by the Cloud Tenant Portal user during node creation.

Customers requiring an operating system image with a different root disk size should work with Singtel to define and make the appropriate OS Image available through Paragon.

Important: The OS Image configuration and the underlying operating system template must be prepared consistently. The Root Volume Size configured in Paragon should correspond to the root disk configuration of the operating system image provided for deployment.

To create a new OS Image, click Create on the OS Images page.

Complete the OS Image configuration using the following fields:
98b40764-b7e8-5552-90d3-063974494058.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Creating an OS Image
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p017_1.png

56846478-d51c-578a-919d-352323048cad.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Creating an OS Image
Complete the OS Image configuration using the following fields:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Enter a unique and descriptive name for the OS Image. |
| Provider | Select the service provider with which the image will be associated. |
| Region | Select the region in which the image will be available. The available options are based on the selected Provider. |
| Zone | Select the zone or zones in which the image will be available. |
| Type | Select the operating system type. |
| Distribution | Select the operating system distribution. |
| OS Version | Enter the operating system version represented by the image. |
| Template ID | Enter the identifier of the underlying image template used for provisioning. |
| Root Volume Size | Enter the root volume capacity required by the OS Image. |
| Mark as K8s Cluster OS Image | Enable this option when the image is intended for Kubernetes cluster creation. |

After entering the required configuration, click Submit to create the OS Image. Click Cancel to return without creating it.

A newly created OS Image is placed in a Disabled state. The Multi-Cloud Administrator must activate the image before it becomes available to CTP users for provisioning.
56846478-d51c-578a-919d-352323048cad.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Creating an OS Image

d743661b-73aa-517e-92fc-34db42f24612.text:

d743661b-73aa-517e-92fc-34db42f24612.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Image Details

f32f6236-909d-57b6-b26a-22ee589b1bd4.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Editing an OS Image
After an OS Image has been created, the PCA can modify its Name. The remaining OS Image configuration cannot be changed through the Edit function.

To edit an OS Image:

1. Select the checkbox beside the required OS Image.
2. Open the Action menu and select Edit.
3. Enter the new name for the OS Image.
4. Click Submit to save the change.

The Private Cloud Administrator is responsible for creating the Regions used to organize resources within the platform.

Private Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones
A Zone is an isolated physical location within a cloud region that contains one or more data centers. Zones are designed to provide high availability and fault tolerance by operating independently from other zones within the same Region.

Zones are associated with a Region and provide the infrastructure endpoints and network configuration required for resources operating within that location.

The PCA can place an individual cluster member into Maintenance Mode using the toggle displayed against the server.

When Maintenance Mode is enabled, the server is excluded from placement of new Virtual Machines. Virtual Machines that are already running on the server are not affected and remain on the server.

This allows the PCA to prevent additional workloads from being placed on a particular cluster member without disrupting existing workloads.

The server's status changes to Maintenance while Maintenance Mode is enabled. Disabling Maintenance Mode returns the server to normal availability for new VM placement.

683a0ae3-5abf-573c-ac03-9f686987e466.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > Network > Elastic IP Pools
An Elastic IP Pool is a collection of pre-allocated static IPv4 addresses that are available for assignment to resources within a specific scope. Each pool defines an address range and the network configuration required for those addresses to be used by platform resources.

Elastic IP Pools can be created for Virtual Machine, Bare Metal, or K8aaS resources. The pool Type determines whether the addresses are Public, for internet-facing connectivity, or Private, for internal network use.

Elastic IP Pools are associated with a specific Region and Zone and cannot be shared across Regions or Zones.

8024abcf-d738-5df5-9edc-94ffdae617c0.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images
For BMaaS, an OS Image is a predefined operating system template that can be deployed onto an allocated bare-metal server. OS Images allow supported operating systems and versions to be registered in Paragon and subsequently made available for server deployment.

The Private Cloud Administrator is responsible for creating and maintaining the OS Images used by BMaaS. Newly created OS Images are Disabled by default and must be activated by the Multi-Cloud Administrator before they become available to CTP users.

Viewing OS Images
The OS Images page provides a searchable list of the operating system images configured for BMaaS. The Search field can be used to locate a specific image.

The table displays the following information:
8024abcf-d738-5df5-9edc-94ffdae617c0.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images

Complete the OS Image configuration using the following fields:
5da9185e-cf05-597c-901f-184a4ec7e19c.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images > Creating an OS Image

242d39eb-5d15-54ff-9099-8ef81ced8e02.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images > Editing an OS Image
After an OS Image has been created, the PCA can modify its Name. The remaining OS Image configuration cannot be changed through the Edit function.

1. Select the checkbox beside the required OS Image.
2. Open the Action menu and select Edit.
3. Enter the new name for the OS Image.
4. Click Submit to save the change.

174a6511-3fb3-5c72-b276-a1ae511df899.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers
A Bare Metal Server is a non-virtualized physical server provisioned for use by a single tenant. The operating system is installed directly on the physical hardware, providing access to the server's CPU, memory, storage, and networking resources without a virtualization layer or resource sharing between tenants.

The Private Cloud Administrator is responsible for onboarding physical servers into Paragon, configuring the required network and boot resources, and activating the servers so that they can subsequently be allocated for tenant use.

Server Lifecycle
A bare-metal server progresses through several states as it moves from initial onboarding to tenant deployment.
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p047_1.png

54bbb1a7-5d81-548f-a601-6fc417f9359c.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Lifecycle
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Commissioning | Paragon is commissioning and preparing the newly onboarded physical server. |
| Commissioned | Commissioning has completed successfully. The server requires its pre- activation configuration before it can be made available for use. |
| Ready | The server has completed PCA onboarding and activation. The server must subsequently be activated by the MCA before it becomes available for allocation to a CTP user. |
| Allocated | The server has been claimed by a CTP user, but an operating system has not yet been deployed. |
| Deployed | The server has been allocated to a CTP user and an operating system has been deployed. |
54bbb1a7-5d81-548f-a601-6fc417f9359c.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Lifecycle

1311b9e5-1552-52b7-8421-b75cfa3bff8c.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Lifecycle
The server Status and Power Status represent separate aspects of the server. Status represents the server's position in the BMaaS lifecycle, while Power Status indicates whether the physical server is currently powered on or off. For example, a server can be in the Ready state while its Power Status is Off.

Viewing Servers
The Servers page provides a searchable list of the bare-metal servers managed through Paragon. The Search field can be used to locate a specific server, while Show Deleted can be enabled to include deleted server records.

The table displays the following information:
1311b9e5-1552-52b7-8421-b75cfa3bff8c.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Lifecycle

681fdfe3-fb75-51a8-b464-d26441e7267a.text:

b8dbea25-96b9-5dc6-81a5-dd0e28964bdf.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Viewing Servers
The Server Size, Region, and Zone are displayed as links and can be selected to access information about the corresponding resources.

Onboarding a Server

To onboard a new bare-metal server, click Onboard on the Servers page.

The Create Server wizard consists of three stages: Resource Details, Server Details, and Review.

Resource Details
The Resource Details stage identifies where the physical server will be onboarded.
b8dbea25-96b9-5dc6-81a5-dd0e28964bdf.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Viewing Servers
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p049_1.png

Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Resource Details
| Field | Description |

a7914938-245f-53e8-a674-466cd58d590c.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Resource Details

33605d49-7c08-55cc-8d04-a29404036f97.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Details
The Server Details stage identifies the physical server, assigns its hardware profile, and provides the management interface information required by Paragon to manage the server.
33605d49-7c08-55cc-8d04-a29404036f97.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Details

ad7e80f4-5d3d-58d1-acec-1400ee864367.text:

2d2d7423-b309-5f58-8895-2284cb2e0e7a.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Review

Click Submit to begin onboarding the server. Use Back if any of the configuration needs to be changed before submission.

8b1d72ab-23e6-5d79-9aac-3e848bbc2cd9.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Commissioning the Server
After the onboarding request is submitted, the server enters the Commissioning state while Paragon prepares and validates the physical server.

No activation should be attempted while commissioning is in progress. Once commissioning has completed successfully, the server transitions to Commissioned.

A Commissioned server is not yet available for tenant allocation. Before it can be activated, the PCA must:

1. Create a bond interface.
2. Select the boot drive.

These requirements are also displayed on the Server Details page for a Commissioned server.

Preparing a Server for Activation
To prepare the Commissioned server, open its Server Details page by clicking the Server Name.

The lower section of the page provides the Network Interfaces, Storage, and Devices tabs containing the hardware information discovered during commissioning.
8b1d72ab-23e6-5d79-9aac-3e848bbc2cd9.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Commissioning the Server
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p051_1.png

30778340-cca0-56cd-a890-c4ad42f22694.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Creating the Bond Interface
The Network Interfaces tab lists the physical network interfaces discovered on the server.

The table displays the interface name, link/interface speed, interface type, and MAC address.

For the bond interface, select the physical interfaces that show a non-zero link speed. These indicate the interfaces with an active network link.

After selecting the required interfaces, click Create Bond.

The confirmation window displays the physical interfaces that will be combined into the bond. Review the selected interfaces and click Create to create the bond.

Once created, the bond is displayed in the Network Interfaces list together with its member interfaces.
30778340-cca0-56cd-a890-c4ad42f22694.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Creating the Bond Interface
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p052_1.png

577fd848-c661-5219-9ff7-b9adbdc282e6.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Selecting the Boot Drive
Open the Storage tab to view the storage devices discovered during commissioning.

The Storage table provides information about each detected disk, including its name, model, capacity, type, boot designation, and serial number.

Identify the disk that will be used as the operating system boot drive. Open the action menu for that disk and select Set Boot Drive.

Review the selected disk and click Set Boot Drive to confirm the selection.

The selected disk is then designated as the server's boot drive and will be used for operating system deployment.
577fd848-c661-5219-9ff7-b9adbdc282e6.section_path: Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Selecting the Boot Drive
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p052_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p053_1.png

80caa6f8-c6ce-598c-b876-3178a1fa8031.text:
Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Activating the Server
Once the bond interface has been created and a boot drive has been selected, the server is ready for activation.

The Activate button is available from the Server Details page.

Click Activate and review the server information displayed in the confirmation window.

Click Activate to confirm the operation.

After successful activation, the server transitions from Commissioned to Ready.

A server in the Ready state has completed the PCA onboarding and preparation process. As with other resources created or onboarded by the PCA, the server must subsequently be activated by the Multi-Cloud Administrator before it becomes available for allocation to CTP users.

The PCA can control the power state of an onboarded server through the Action menu on the Servers page.

Private Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Deleting a Server
The availability of the Delete action depends on the current lifecycle state of the server.

The PCA cannot delete servers that are in the Ready or Deployed state. This prevents servers that have been made available for allocation or that are already deployed for tenant use from being removed directly through the PCA interface.

Where deletion is available, select the server and choose Delete from the Action menu. Deleted server records can be included in the Servers list by enabling Show Deleted.

2006f8e6-d266-5bfb-9adc-86d54a23bbeb.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator
The Multi Cloud Administrator (MCA) is responsible for managing and orchestrating resources across multiple cloud environments and infrastructure providers within Paragon. The role operates at a platform level across providers and regions, with visibility into resources spanning multiple organisations and subscriptions.

The MCA manages the availability and configuration of platform resources exposed to tenants, including compute resources, Kubernetes services, networking, storage and bare metal services. The role also provides administrative oversight of resource allocation and tenant policies, including the review and approval of resource limit requests.

Through the MCA portal, administrators can monitor platform resources, manage their availability to tenants, review operational transactions, and perform administrative actions required to support the delivery of cloud services across the Paragon environment.

This section describes the functions available to the MCA and follows the structure of the Paragon navigation interface.

5e6d3f9f-7a06-5993-84f0-19471ca9086b.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Dashboard
The Dashboard is the default page displayed when the Multi-Cloud Administrator (MCA) logs in to Paragon. It provides a consolidated overview of the cloud resources and services managed through the platform, allowing the MCA to quickly assess resource availability, utilization states, and recent platform activity.

Resource Overview
The upper section of the Dashboard provides summary counts for key resources managed within Paragon.
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p057_1.png

fc33b829-feee-5eb5-bb11-e2cca8cfc936.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Dashboard > Resource Overview
| Resource | Description |
|---|---|

| Regions | Total number of Regions available across the configured providers. |
| Zones | Total number of Zones available within the platform. |
| Organizations | Total number of organizations configured in Paragon. |
fc33b829-feee-5eb5-bb11-e2cca8cfc936.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Dashboard > Resource Overview

38c68c3a-3708-50ce-b877-26839859904b.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Dashboard > Resource Status
The Dashboard provides status summaries for several resource types.

Virtual Machines displays the total number of virtual machines and groups them by their current state, including Running, Stopped, and Others.

Subnets displays the total number of subnets and categorizes them as Available or Others.

Elastic IP Pools displays the total number of Elastic IP Pools and categorizes them as Available or Others.

Elastic IPs displays the total number of Elastic IP addresses and categorizes them as Available, In Use, or Others.

These summaries provide the MCA with an at-a-glance view of the current state and availability of commonly managed cloud resources.

Connectivity and Network Summary
The Dashboard also provides summary information for additional network and connectivity resources.
38c68c3a-3708-50ce-b877-26839859904b.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Dashboard > Resource Status
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p057_2.png

1124b1e9-2ea4-5652-9a49-5d0a6a627570.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs
The Transaction Logs page provides the MCA with a record of administrative and resource operations performed across organizations and subscriptions within Paragon. Unlike the PCA view, the MCA can filter transactions by Organization and Subscription, providing visibility across the resources under MCA administration.

| Details | Opens the detailed transaction information. |
97be2f44-cdf7-51cc-b6e8-d82b8c52c2bd.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > Searching and Filtering Transactions

15360b9e-60f0-50fe-b28c-3aeffa21312b.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > Viewing Transaction Details
Click the information icon under Details for the required transaction to open the Transaction Details window.

The Transaction Details window provides additional information about the selected operation, including the request description, transaction type, start and end times, user, user organization, creation and update times, trace ID, and associated organization information.

The transaction status is also displayed prominently at the top of the window, allowing the MCA to quickly determine whether the operation completed successfully.

Where Linked Resources are available, the corresponding control can be used to access the resources associated with the transaction.
15360b9e-60f0-50fe-b28c-3aeffa21312b.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > Viewing Transaction Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p061_1.png

98f32704-996a-5ef8-aff4-370754c43373.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute
The Compute section provides the Multi-Cloud Administrator (MCA) with visibility and administrative control over the compute resources available across Paragon. It includes the compute instances provisioned by tenant users, the resource configurations made available for provisioning, and the underlying provider, Region, and Zone structure.

For the MCA, the Compute section contains Nodes, Node Sizes, OS Images, Providers, Regions, and Zones.

03aed7a7-4d97-5579-987b-24279fd7898e.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes
Nodes are virtualized compute resources provisioned for tenant use across the providers, Regions, and Zones available through Paragon.

The MCA view provides visibility across organizations and subscriptions, allowing the administrator to inspect provisioned virtual machines and their associated compute, network, storage, security, and activity information.
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p062_1.png

2eb7fa1e-b68b-5c68-99e1-9e4e65f9f653.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Nodes
The Compute Nodes page provides Organization and Subscription filters for narrowing the displayed resources to a particular tenant context. The Search field can be used to locate a specific Node, while Show Deleted can be enabled to include deleted records.

The table provides information including the Node name and hostname, assigned Node Size, private and Elastic IP addresses, GPU configuration, Zone, Region, and associated provider.

Several resource names displayed in the table are links, allowing the MCA to navigate to information about the corresponding Node Size, Zone, Region, or provider.

The MCA does not perform lifecycle actions on Nodes from this page. The available Action option provides access to the detailed view of the selected Node.
2eb7fa1e-b68b-5c68-99e1-9e4e65f9f653.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Nodes

264857c9-d751-5e3b-b3cb-51cbca3f1196.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Node Details
To view a Node, click its Name directly from the Compute Nodes table. Alternatively, select the required Node and choose View More from the Action menu.

The Compute Node Details page provides information about the selected virtual machine, including its identity, assigned resources, network addressing, location, and current status.
264857c9-d751-5e3b-b3cb-51cbca3f1196.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Node Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p063_1.png

3e00afaf-8b32-5fd7-bcb4-0642bddfc35d.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Node Details
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| UUID | Unique system-generated identifier for the Node. |
| Name | Name assigned to the Node. |
| Host Name | Hostname assigned to the virtual machine. |
| Username | Username associated with the virtual machine. |
| GPU | Indicates whether GPU resources are assigned. |
| Node Size | Node Size used to provision the virtual machine. |
| Private IP | Private IP address assigned to the Node. |
| Image | OS Image used to provision the virtual machine. |
| Provider | Provider through which the Node is provisioned. |
| Region | Region in which the Node is located. |
| Zone | Zone in which the Node is located. |
| Status | Current status of the Node. |
| Created At | Date and time at which the Node was created. |
| Updated At | Date and time at which the Node was last updated. |
3e00afaf-8b32-5fd7-bcb4-0642bddfc35d.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Viewing Node Details

573b4b0b-3bc1-5ede-8c87-49621372834c.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Node Resource Information
The lower section of the Compute Node Details page provides additional information through the Network Interfaces, Storage, Security, and History tabs.

The Network Interfaces tab displays the network interfaces associated with the Node, including the primary interface created during provisioning and any additional interfaces subsequently attached to the virtual machine. Network information includes the subnet IP address, MAC address, associated subnet, and Elastic IP information where applicable.

The Storage tab displays the storage attached to the Node. This includes the root volume used by the virtual machine as well as any additional storage volumes that have been attached. Information such as volume name, size, type, root-volume designation, attachment status, and attachment time is provided.

The Security tab provides the access information associated with the Node, including the username, SSH access key name, and key fingerprint.

The History tab provides a record of operations performed on the Node. This includes the transaction description and ID, start and end times, status, initiating user, and linked resources where applicable.
573b4b0b-3bc1-5ede-8c87-49621372834c.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Node Resource Information
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p064_1.png

ca959b43-78c8-5fa3-b14c-a60a724e9264.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes
Node Sizes define the compute profiles available for provisioning virtual machines, including the CPU, memory, and GPU configuration associated with each profile.

Within the MCA interface, Node Sizes created by the PCA can be reviewed and their availability controlled before they are exposed for downstream consumption.

Viewing Node Sizes
The Node Sizes page provides a searchable list of the Node Sizes available to the MCA.

The table displays the following information:
ca959b43-78c8-5fa3-b14c-a60a724e9264.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p065_1.png

27602260-cd33-5a65-a116-9390844b3439.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Viewing Node Sizes
The table displays the following information:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the Node Size. |
| Service Provider | Service provider associated with the Node Size. |
| Region | Region in which the Node Size is configured. |
| CPU | Number of CPU cores defined by the Node Size. |
| Memory (GB) | Memory capacity defined by the Node Size. |
| Status | Current availability status of the Node Size. |

The Name and Region are displayed as links and can be selected to access the corresponding resource information.
27602260-cd33-5a65-a116-9390844b3439.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Viewing Node Sizes

0faacd2f-1883-506e-b40c-e1da7a47fe4a.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Node Size Status
The MCA controls whether a Node Size is enabled for downstream consumption. A Node Size can have the following statuses:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The Node Size has not previously been activated by the MCA. |
| Enabled | The Node Size has been activated by the MCA and is enabled for downstream use. |
| Disabled | The Node Size was previously enabled and has subsequently been disabled by the MCA. |

A newly created Node Size received from the PCA therefore progresses from Pending to Enabled when it is first activated. An Enabled Node Size can subsequently be changed to Disabled.
0faacd2f-1883-506e-b40c-e1da7a47fe4a.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Node Size Status

f48e974a-fd3e-50de-92af-0d7eb051de77.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Activating and Disabling a Node Size
To change the availability of a Node Size, select the checkbox beside the required Node Size and open the Action menu.

For a Node Size in the Pending or Disabled state, select Activate to enable it.

For a Node Size in the Enabled state, select Disable to prevent it from being made available for downstream consumption.

The available option in the Action menu depends on the current status of the selected Node Size.

Synchronizing Node Sizes
The Sync function synchronizes the Node Size information available to the MCA with the underlying platform resource information.

Click Sync from the Node Sizes page to initiate synchronization.

Viewing Node Size Details
Click the Name of a Node Size to open its detailed view.

The Node Size Details page displays the configuration and current status of the selected Node Size.
f48e974a-fd3e-50de-92af-0d7eb051de77.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Activating and Disabling a Node Size
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p066_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p067_1.png

3dc7c365-c6d6-59cd-b11b-2e572a23fd52.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Viewing Node Size Details
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the Node Size. |
| UUID | Unique system-generated identifier for the Node Size. |
| Service Provider | Service provider associated with the Node Size. |
| Region | Region in which the Node Size is configured. |
| CPU | Number of CPU cores defined by the Node Size. |
| Memory | Memory capacity defined by the Node Size. |
| GPU Enabled | Indicates whether the Node Size includes GPU resources. |
| Status | Current MCA availability status of the Node Size. |
| Created At | Date and time at which the Node Size was created. |
| Updated At | Date and time at which the Node Size was last updated. |

The lower section lists the Zones associated with the Node Size, including the Zone Name and corresponding Zone UUID.
3dc7c365-c6d6-59cd-b11b-2e572a23fd52.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Node Sizes > Viewing Node Size Details

897c6d54-2320-5d49-9fdc-44c939d3a467.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images
OS Images define the operating system templates available for provisioning virtual machines in Paragon. They contain the operating system information and configuration required when creating a new compute instance.

Within the MCA interface, OS Images created by the PCA can be reviewed and their availability controlled before they are exposed for downstream consumption.

Viewing OS Images
The OS Images page provides a searchable list of the OS Images available to the MCA.

The table displays the following information:
897c6d54-2320-5d49-9fdc-44c939d3a467.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p068_1.png

2c1f75bc-f789-5ef8-b78b-5118d1f71213.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Images
The table displays the following information:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the OS Image. |
| Type | Operating system type, such as Linux or Windows. |
| Distribution | Operating system distribution associated with the image. |
| Root Volume Size | Root volume capacity configured for the OS Image. |
| Status | Current availability status of the OS Image. |
2c1f75bc-f789-5ef8-b78b-5118d1f71213.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Images

83e63bae-24e0-5ce9-837c-156f8ca9aa05.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > OS Image Status
As with Node Sizes, the MCA controls whether an OS Image is enabled for downstream consumption.
83e63bae-24e0-5ce9-837c-156f8ca9aa05.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > OS Image Status

9bea42d0-94fb-58fc-9ff7-ce8ea798aee2.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > OS Image Status
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The OS Image has not previously been activated by the MCA. |
| Enabled | The OS Image has been activated by the MCA and is enabled for downstream use. |
| Disabled | The OS Image was previously enabled and has subsequently been disabled by the MCA. |

A newly created OS Image received from the PCA progresses from Pending to Enabled when it is first activated. An Enabled OS Image can subsequently be changed to Disabled.
9bea42d0-94fb-58fc-9ff7-ce8ea798aee2.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > OS Image Status

0a3c8ed5-4381-5ae9-a223-b119b9294490.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Activating and Disabling an OS Image
To change the availability of an OS Image, select the checkbox beside the required image and open the Action menu.

For an OS Image in the Pending or Disabled state, select Activate to enable it.

For an OS Image in the Enabled state, select Disable to prevent it from being made available for downstream consumption.

The available option in the Action menu depends on the current status of the selected OS Image.

The Activate OS Image page allows the MCA to define the tenancy of the OS Image before making it available for downstream consumption.

The Tenancy setting determines how the OS Image is made available:
0a3c8ed5-4381-5ae9-a223-b119b9294490.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Activating and Disabling an OS Image
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p069_1.png

ded5105a-f851-5768-9d3d-4732715144ae.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Activating and Disabling an OS Image
The Tenancy setting determines how the OS Image is made available:
| Tenancy | Description |
|---|---|
| SHARED | Makes the OS Image available across subscriptions. |
| DEDICATED | Restricts the OS Image to specifically selected organizations and subscriptions. |
ded5105a-f851-5768-9d3d-4732715144ae.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Activating and Disabling an OS Image

4b64bc39-b53d-5a26-bb30-c65c2f78ec8c.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Activating and Disabling an OS Image
When SHARED is selected, click Submit to activate the OS Image with shared availability.

When DEDICATED is selected, the Allowed Subscription section is displayed. Click + Subscription to select the organization and subscription that should be permitted to use the OS Image. Additional allowed subscriptions can be associated with the image as required.

Synchronizing OS Images
The Sync function synchronizes the OS Image information available to the MCA with the underlying platform resource information.

Click Sync from the OS Images page to initiate synchronization.

Viewing OS Image Details
Click the Name of an OS Image to open its detailed view.

The OS Image Details page displays the configuration and current availability of the selected image.
4b64bc39-b53d-5a26-bb30-c65c2f78ec8c.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Activating and Disabling an OS Image
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p069_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p071_1.png

be2343ca-c5ee-5e33-a8a5-0d0b2e1b7a28.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Image Details
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the OS Image. |
| UUID | Unique system-generated identifier for the OS Image. |
| Provider | Service provider associated with the OS Image. |
| Region | Region in which the OS Image is configured. |
| Tenancy | Indicates how the OS Image is made available across subscriptions. |
| Type | Operating system type associated with the image. |
| Distribution | Operating system distribution associated with the image. |
| OS Version | Operating system version represented by the image. |
| Root Volume Size | Root volume capacity configured for instances created using the image. |
| Is For K8s Cluster Creation | Indicates whether the OS Image is designated for Kubernetes cluster creation. |
| Status | Current availability status of the OS Image. |
