| Updated At | Date and time at which the OS Image was last updated. |

The Tenancy information identifies how the image is made available. For example, an image with SHARED tenancy is shared across subscriptions, as indicated on the details page.
be2343ca-c5ee-5e33-a8a5-0d0b2e1b7a28.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > OS Images > Viewing OS Image Details

1100300c-639a-51ad-a55a-d4b78fcde4ae.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Providers
A Provider represents an organization or service that supplies the underlying computing infrastructure used to deliver cloud resources through Paragon. Providers enable infrastructure and services to be organized and managed through a common platform abstraction.

Within the MCA interface, Providers establish the service provider context under which Regions and the associated cloud resources are managed.

Viewing Providers
The Providers page displays the Providers configured in Paragon. The Search field can be used to locate a specific Provider.

The table displays the following information:
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p072_1.png

8259321a-1523-584a-9695-39e1fb19a750.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Providers > Viewing Providers
The table displays the following information:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the Provider. |
| Service Provider Type | Type of service provided, such as private cloud infrastructure. |
| Service Provider | Underlying service provider associated with the Provider. |

The Name is displayed as a link and can be selected to access the Provider information.
8259321a-1523-584a-9695-39e1fb19a750.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Providers > Viewing Providers

1eaf7a10-9244-5b7a-ad26-5db4a95398f0.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Providers > Creating a Provider
To create a Provider:

1. Click Create from the Providers page.
2. Enter a Name for the Provider.
3. Select the required Service Provider.
4. Click Submit to create the Provider.

The Service Provider selection identifies the underlying infrastructure service with which the Provider is associated.

Editing a Provider
The MCA can modify the name assigned to an existing Provider.

To edit a Provider:

1. Select the checkbox beside the required Provider.
2. Open the Action menu.
3. Select Edit.
4. Enter the required Name.
5. Click Submit to save the change.

Only the Provider Name can be modified after creation.

Viewing Provider Details
Click the Name of a Provider from the Providers table to open the detailed view.

The Provider Details page displays additional information about the selected Provider, including its Name, UUID, Service Provider Type, and associated Service Provider.
1eaf7a10-9244-5b7a-ad26-5db4a95398f0.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Providers > Creating a Provider
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p073_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p073_2.png

d78580c8-8041-556c-ae97-92737709cd96.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions
A Region is a geographic area that contains one or more data centers where a cloud provider hosts and delivers cloud services. Regions provide the geographic structure within which Zones and their associated infrastructure resources are organized.

Regions are created at the PCA level and made available to the MCA for activation.

Viewing Regions
The Regions page provides a searchable list of Regions available to the MCA.

The table displays the following information:
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p074_1.png

41f0db97-3b26-5d9f-925b-8bccbc21c07e.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions > Viewing Regions
The table displays the following information:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the Region. |
| Service Provider | Service provider associated with the Region. |
| Status | Current status of the Region. |

A newly created Region is initially displayed with a Pending status and must be activated by the MCA before it becomes active.
41f0db97-3b26-5d9f-925b-8bccbc21c07e.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions > Viewing Regions

1e7decc2-6020-5338-808c-76d64f0280fc.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions > Activating a Region
To activate a Region:

1. Select the checkbox beside the required Region.
2. Open the Action menu.
3. Select Activate.

Following successful activation, the Region status changes from Pending to Active.

Unlike resources such as Node Sizes and OS Images, an Active Region cannot subsequently be deactivated through the MCA interface.

Synchronizing Regions
The Sync function synchronizes the Region information available to the MCA with the underlying platform resource information.

Click Sync from the Regions page to initiate synchronization.

Viewing Region Details
Click the Name of a Region to open its detailed view.

The Region Details page displays the following information:
1e7decc2-6020-5338-808c-76d64f0280fc.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions > Activating a Region
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p075_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p075_2.png

273e3668-34f0-59bf-8176-6e5aca95fb24.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions > Viewing Region Details
The Region Details page displays the following information:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Name assigned to the Region. |
| UUID | Unique system-generated identifier for the Region. |
| Service Provider | Service provider associated with the Region. |
| Status | Current status of the Region. |
| Created At | Date and time at which the Region was created. |
| Updated At | Date and time at which the Region was last updated. |
273e3668-34f0-59bf-8176-6e5aca95fb24.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Regions > Viewing Region Details

107b5f91-0d57-52ef-a21f-c737ad449cb4.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones
A Zone is an isolated physical location within a Region that contains the infrastructure resources used to deliver cloud services. Zones are created by the PCA and must be activated by the MCA before they can be used by the platform.

The Zones page displays the Zones available to the MCA together with their associated Region and current status.

The following statuses may be displayed:
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p076_1.png

5e45b3e5-a880-5d1d-b583-67beba27d3ed.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones
The following statuses may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The Zone has been created but has not yet been activated by the MCA. |
| Active | The Zone has been activated and is available for use. |

28b9fd7a-0356-5e87-b512-b544968e1df0.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > Activating a Zone
To activate a Zone:

1. Select the checkbox beside the required Zone.
2. Open the Action menu.
3. Select Activate.

Synchronizing Zones
The Sync function synchronizes the Zone information available to the MCA with the underlying platform resource information.

Click Sync from the Zone page to initiate synchronization.
28b9fd7a-0356-5e87-b512-b544968e1df0.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > Activating a Zone

69444c0e-60e3-5c25-8b4c-c7751d1a85d6.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > Viewing Zone Details
Click the Zone Name to open the Zone Details page.

The Zone Details page displays the Zone's core information, including its Name, UUID, Service Provider, associated Region, and creation and update timestamps.

The page also shows the tenancy configuration for the Zone. For a SHARED Zone, the Zone is available across tenants rather than being restricted to a specific tenant.

K8aaS Configuration
For Zones that support Kubernetes as a Service (K8aaS), the K8aaS Config section defines the infrastructure resources that K8aaS uses when provisioning Kubernetes clusters within that Zone.

The configuration is divided into three areas:
69444c0e-60e3-5c25-8b4c-c7751d1a85d6.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > Viewing Zone Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p077_1.png

bb1014b0-a7f5-555f-9819-912c8a28f988.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > K8aaS Configuration
The configuration is divided into three areas:
| Configuration | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Network | Defines the Elastic IP Pool and Virtual Network used by K8aaS. Configuration |
| OS Image Configuration | Defines the OS Images used for the Master Node, VM Node, Bare Metal Node, and Load Balancer. |
| Storage | Defines the Storage Pool used by K8aaS workloads in the Zone. Configuration |

The current configuration is displayed directly on the Zone Details page.
bb1014b0-a7f5-555f-9819-912c8a28f988.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > K8aaS Configuration
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p077_2.png

7a54fc33-0f40-517f-83b8-f030e4d2ca41.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > Editing the K8aaS Configuration
Select Edit from the K8aaS Config section to modify the Kubernetes configuration associated with the Zone.

The following settings can be configured:

Network Configuration
• Elastic IP Pool – Select the Elastic IP Pool to be used by K8aaS. • Virtual Network – Select the Virtual Network to be used by K8aaS.

OS Image Configuration
• Master Node – Select the OS Image used for Kubernetes master nodes. • VM Node – Select the OS Image used for virtual machine worker nodes. • BM Node – Select the OS Image used for bare metal worker nodes. • Load Balancer – Select the OS Image used for the K8aaS load balancer.

Storage Configuration
• Storage Pool – Select the Storage Pool to be used by K8aaS.

After completing the required changes, select Update Changes to save the configuration.

Disabling K8aaS Configuration
The Disable option shown within the K8aaS Config section is separate from the overall status of the Zone. It applies to the K8aaS configuration associated with that Zone rather than deactivating the Zone itself.
7a54fc33-0f40-517f-83b8-f030e4d2ca41.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Zones > Editing the K8aaS Configuration
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p078_1.png

00a17fac-3c17-5d59-8f23-0912a8e0c499.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters
The Kubernetes Clusters page allows the MCA to view Kubernetes clusters provisioned across tenant organisations and subscriptions. The page provides information including the Cluster Name, Organisation, Subscription, Kubernetes Version, Region, Resource Group, creation time, and current Status.

The Organisation and Subscription filters can be used to narrow the displayed clusters, while the Search field can be used to locate a specific cluster.

Select the Cluster Name directly from the table to open the detailed view.

Alternatively, select the required cluster, open the Action menu, and select View More.
00a17fac-3c17-5d59-8f23-0912a8e0c499.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p079_1.png

3d419f38-c712-59ab-a027-f27a51886953.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Kubernetes Cluster Details
The Kubernetes Cluster Details page provides detailed information about the selected cluster, including its cluster endpoint, status, organisation, subscription, Kubernetes version, provider, region, zone, resource group, and creation information.

Additional information is available through the tabs at the bottom of the page:

• Control Plane displays the control plane configuration and the individual control plane nodes, including their hostname, IP address, role, and status. • Worker Node displays the configured worker groups and their provisioned worker nodes. • Other Members displays supporting cluster components such as the API server, load balancers, ingress components, and VIPs. • Kubernetes Cluster Requests displays operations performed for the cluster, including cluster creation and worker node operations. • Network Resources displays the network resources associated with the cluster, including subnets, Elastic IPs, Node Connects, NAT Gateways, network routes, and network policies.
3d419f38-c712-59ab-a027-f27a51886953.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Kubernetes Cluster Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p079_2.png

bb5204cd-6009-5e9a-a7ef-97e98d75018c.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Viewing the Kubernetes Processing Workflow
The MCA can view the processing workflow associated with a Kubernetes cluster operation from the Kubernetes Cluster Requests tab.

To view a workflow:

1. Select the Kubernetes Cluster Requests tab.
2. Locate the required request.
3. Select View Workflow.

The K8aaS Processing Workflow page displays the individual tasks performed as part of the selected operation and their current processing state. Tasks are identified as Pending, Running, Completed, Failed, or other states.

The Reload button can be used to refresh the workflow and display the latest processing state.
bb5204cd-6009-5e9a-a7ef-97e98d75018c.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Viewing the Kubernetes Processing Workflow
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p080_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p081_1.png

3668b956-6d47-58ba-89d0-9879f8b1cd84.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Retrying a Failed Workflow Task
If a Kubernetes operation contains a failed workflow task, the MCA can retry the failed task from the K8aaS Processing Workflow page.

Select the failed task in the workflow to display its Workflow Details, including the Task Type, Status, processing information, and available error message.

Select Retry to retry the failed task.

Note: Where multiple workflow tasks have failed, each failed task must be reviewed and retried individually. Retrying one failed task does not automatically retry the other failed tasks in the workflow.
3668b956-6d47-58ba-89d0-9879f8b1cd84.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Retrying a Failed Workflow Task
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p081_2.png

d114f2fa-530f-5b36-a665-707806d6fa7c.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking
The Networking section allows the Multi Cloud Admin (MCA) to manage and oversee the network resources used to provide connectivity to workloads within Paragon. The MCA defines the logical network structure, controls the availability of IP address resources, and maintains visibility into the subnets created for tenant use.

For the MCA, the Networking section contains Virtual Networks, Elastic IP Pools, and Subnets.

b1ba2290-3431-58ea-9c53-6e9c58f9420d.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Virtual Networks
Virtual Networks provide the logical network address space used by resources deployed within Paragon. Each Virtual Network is associated with a provider and region and defines an IPv4 CIDR range from which network resources can be created.

Virtual Networks can be configured for Virtual Machine, Bare Metal, or K8aaS workloads. The network type determines the category of resources for which the Virtual Network is intended.

The Virtual Networks page displays the configured networks and provides information including the network name, CIDR range, current usage, type, and status. The Usage column shows the number of network slices currently consumed against the total available capacity. A network whose available capacity has been fully consumed is displayed with a Full status.

To view additional information, click the Virtual Network name directly. Alternatively, select the Virtual Network and choose Action > View More.

The Virtual Network Details page displays the network configuration, including the provider, region, network type, IPv4 CIDR, slice prefix, current usage, and status. The Subnets Attached section lists the subnets created from the Virtual Network, together with their associated organization, subscription, IPv4 range, usage, and VLAN information.

Creating a Virtual Network
To create a Virtual Network, click Create from the Virtual Networks page.

Configure the following information:

Field Description
b1ba2290-3431-58ea-9c53-6e9c58f9420d.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Virtual Networks
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p082_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p083_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p083_2.png

4e0ea1ab-8c88-5724-aaf8-a6e9eced7292.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Virtual Networks > Creating a Virtual Network
| Name | Enter a name for the Virtual Network. |
|---|---|
| Provider | Select the provider under which the network will be created. |
| Region | Select the region for the Virtual Network. |
| Type | Select the intended workload type: Virtual Machine, Bare Metal, or K8aaS. |
| CIDR | Enter the IPv4 CIDR block allocated to the Virtual Network. |
| Slice Setting | Specify the prefix used when dividing the Virtual Network address space into subnet ranges. |

Click Submit to create the Virtual Network.
4e0ea1ab-8c88-5724-aaf8-a6e9eced7292.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Virtual Networks > Creating a Virtual Network

f3a65af2-5b04-51ea-a54c-c44d3a9e658d.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Virtual Networks > Editing and Deleting Virtual Networks
To edit a Virtual Network, select the required network and choose Action > Edit. The Edit function allows the Virtual Network name to be updated.

A Virtual Network can also be deleted through Action > Delete. However, a Virtual Network that has subnets associated with it cannot be deleted. The associated subnets must first be removed before the Virtual Network can be deleted.
f3a65af2-5b04-51ea-a54c-c44d3a9e658d.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Virtual Networks > Editing and Deleting Virtual Networks

e17f0d85-3cbb-50e4-a35f-c6d356acd3c9.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools
Elastic IP Pools are collections of pre-allocated static IPv4 addresses that can be assigned to resources within a defined scope. Each pool defines the address range and network configuration used when allocating Elastic IPs to workloads.

Elastic IP Pools may contain Public addresses for internet-facing connectivity or Private addresses for internal network use. Pools can be configured for Virtual Machine or Bare Metal workloads.

The Elastic IP Pools page displays the configured pools and provides information including the pool name, CIDR, type, category, start and end IP addresses, gateway, VLAN, and current status.

The following statuses may be displayed:
e17f0d85-3cbb-50e4-a35f-c6d356acd3c9.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p084_1.png

903cb46e-11c5-53bf-b419-cf0cb728f26d.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools
The following statuses may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The Elastic IP Pool has been synchronized but has not yet been activated. |
| Active | The Elastic IP Pool is active and available for use. |
| Full | The available addresses within the Elastic IP Pool have been allocated. |
| Deleted | The Elastic IP Pool has been deleted and is no longer available for new allocations. |
903cb46e-11c5-53bf-b419-cf0cb728f26d.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools

15d5655c-309f-5eab-977f-1f8f5de21d2f.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools > Activating an Elastic IP Pool
Elastic IP Pools are synchronized from the underlying platform and must be activated by the MCA before they become available for use.

To activate a pool, select an Elastic IP Pool with a Pending status and choose Action > Activate.

The Activate action is only available where applicable. Once activation is complete, the pool status changes to Active.
15d5655c-309f-5eab-977f-1f8f5de21d2f.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools > Activating an Elastic IP Pool

d75e6640-c0ab-5e59-9c7f-76350586ec50.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools > Viewing Elastic IP Pool Details
Click the Elastic IP Pool name to open its details.

The Elastic Pool Details page provides the complete configuration of the selected pool, including its service provider, tenancy, category, CIDR, VLAN, address range, gateway, status, and creation and update information.

The Elastic IPs section provides visibility into addresses that have been allocated from the pool. For each allocation, the page identifies the Elastic IP address, the organization and subscription to which it was allocated, and the allocation time.
d75e6640-c0ab-5e59-9c7f-76350586ec50.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Elastic IP Pools > Viewing Elastic IP Pool Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p085_1.png

5c98ee90-bbc4-5b89-b802-dd9413664456.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Subnets
A Subnet is a logical subdivision of a Virtual Network that provides a defined range of IP addresses for resources. Subnets are associated with a specific Organization and Subscription and are created from the address space available within the parent Virtual Network.

The Subnets page provides the MCA with visibility across subnets created by tenant organizations and subscriptions. The page displays the subnet name, IPv4 CIDR, current address usage, subnet type, Zone, Region, Organization, Subscription, and current status.

The Usage value indicates the number of addresses currently in use relative to the available address capacity of the subnet.

The following subnet states may be displayed:
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p087_1.png

3dcb7f8a-6198-557b-820d-56fd37d511a0.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Subnets
The following subnet states may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Active | The subnet is available for use. |
| Full | The available addresses within the subnet have been allocated. |
| Deleted | The subnet has been deleted and is no longer available for use. |

de1145da-f37b-5bfb-bd5a-39531ed308e3.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Subnets > Viewing Subnet Details
Click the Subnet Name to open the Subnet Details page.

The details page displays information including the subnet UUID, IPv4 CIDR, Provider, Region, Zone, Subnet Type, associated Virtual Network, usage, status, and creation and update timestamps.

The Usage section identifies resources currently consuming addresses from the subnet and displays the corresponding IP address assigned to each resource.
de1145da-f37b-5bfb-bd5a-39531ed308e3.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Networking > Subnets > Viewing Subnet Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p088_1.png

1210a0f6-fa69-54da-9de1-f315a11fa0c6.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage
The Storage section allows the Multi Cloud Admin (MCA) to manage the storage resources made available through the Paragon platform. From this section, the MCA can view synchronized Storage Pools and control their availability for use by activating eligible pools.

Storage Pools originate from the underlying platform and are synchronized into Paragon before being activated for use.

bc8b60d8-8f7b-5e7a-8c7e-ee47159baca6.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage > Storage Pools
A Storage Pool represents a logical pool of storage capacity available through a service provider. Storage Pools are associated with specific Zones and define the storage type and capacity that can be made available for workloads.

The Storage Pools page provides a consolidated view of the storage pools available to the MCA.

The Storage Pools page displays the available Storage Pools together with their storage type, capacity, tenancy, associated Zone, and current status. The Show Deleted option can be enabled to include Storage Pools that have been deleted.
bc8b60d8-8f7b-5e7a-8c7e-ee47159baca6.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage > Storage Pools
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p089_1.png

8a7c2bf6-36c8-5d1a-9ad6-509726b842d9.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage > Synchronizing Storage Pools
Click Sync to synchronize Storage Pool information from the underlying platform into Paragon. This allows newly available or updated Storage Pools to be reflected in the MCA portal.
8a7c2bf6-36c8-5d1a-9ad6-509726b842d9.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage > Synchronizing Storage Pools

89546d6d-0a17-5892-a9db-e42acb4e0caf.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage > Activating a Storage Pool
Storage Pools must be activated before they are made available for use through the platform.

To activate a Storage Pool:

1. Select the required Storage Pool using the checkbox.
2. Open the Action menu.
3. Click Activate.
89546d6d-0a17-5892-a9db-e42acb4e0caf.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Storage > Activating a Storage Pool

ea75a96a-bac9-5daa-92ed-50c31ea0a1ce.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Connect
The Connect section provides the Multi Cloud Admin (MCA) with visibility into connectivity resources used to provide external access to compute nodes.

For the MCA, the Connect section contains Node Connects.

a0903cc3-95ba-5c36-aa06-49048364fbdf.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Connect > Node Connects
Node Connect provides external connectivity to a compute node by associating an Elastic IP with the node. The Elastic IP used for the connection must be available within the same zone and is dedicated to the Node Connect while it remains assigned.

The Node Connects page provides a consolidated view of configured connections, including the Node Connect name, assigned Elastic IP, attached resource, region, zone, provider, and current status. The MCA can filter the displayed Node Connects by Organization and Subscription, or use the Search field to locate a specific connection.
a0903cc3-95ba-5c36-aa06-49048364fbdf.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Connect > Node Connects
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p090_1.png

8a326d47-2719-54fa-93f6-b4ae3b7b2a61.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Connect > Node Connects > Viewing Node Connect Details
To view additional information for a Node Connect, click the Node Connect name directly.

Alternatively, select the required Node Connect, open the Action menu, and click View More.

The Node Connect Details page displays information about the selected connection, including its name and UUID, allocated Elastic IP, attached resource, provider, region, zone, status, and creation and update timestamps.
8a326d47-2719-54fa-93f6-b4ae3b7b2a61.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Connect > Node Connects > Viewing Node Connect Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p090_2.png

1f3b8f39-3c3b-5d75-98cb-2155732245da.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS
The BMaaS section enables the Multi Cloud Admin (MCA) to manage Bare Metal as a Service resources and control their availability within the platform.

For the MCA, the BMaaS section includes Server Size, OS Image, and Servers.

a11b3b02-7e81-52bc-902c-96a2e070dce6.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size
A Server Size defines the hardware configuration associated with a bare metal server, including its CPU, memory, storage, and, where applicable, GPU resources.

Server Sizes are created and configured by the Private Cloud Admin (PCA). From the MCA portal, these Server Sizes can be reviewed and activated or disabled to control their availability within the platform.

The Server Sizes page displays the Server Size name, service provider, region, server type, CPU, memory, storage, current status, and creation date.
a11b3b02-7e81-52bc-902c-96a2e070dce6.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p091_1.png

ae232140-6504-5edf-89d8-02fc9285f931.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size > Server Size Status
A Server Size can have the following statuses:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The Server Size has been created by the PCA but has not yet been activated by the MCA. |
| Enabled | The Server Size has been activated and is available for use within the platform. |
| Disabled | The Server Size has been disabled by the MCA and is no longer available for new use. |
ae232140-6504-5edf-89d8-02fc9285f931.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size > Server Size Status

9921f3d3-e47d-555d-809e-8cad93aed389.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size > Activating or Disabling a Server Size
To activate a Server Size in Pending or Disabled status, select the required Server Size, open the Action menu, and click Activate.

To disable an Enabled Server Size, select the required Server Size, open the Action menu, and click Disable.

The available action depends on the current status of the selected Server Size.
9921f3d3-e47d-555d-809e-8cad93aed389.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size > Activating or Disabling a Server Size
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p092_1.png

e563d5b3-97fa-5582-851e-bf3800bc2e0e.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size > Viewing Server Size Details
To view additional information for a Server Size, click the Server Size name.

The Server Size Details page provides the complete hardware configuration, including CPU, memory, storage, server type, and GPU configuration where applicable. It also displays the associated service provider, region, zone, status, UUID, and creation and update timestamps.
e563d5b3-97fa-5582-851e-bf3800bc2e0e.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Server Size > Viewing Server Size Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p092_2.png

fe0f4ada-5d5e-5b3f-9c0d-75529278b21b.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images
An OS Image is a predefined operating system image used to deploy an operating system directly onto a bare metal server.

OS Images are created and configured by the Private Cloud Admin (PCA). From the MCA portal, these images can be activated or disabled to control their availability for BMaaS deployments.

The OS Images page displays the image name, type, distribution, OS version, and current status.
fe0f4ada-5d5e-5b3f-9c0d-75529278b21b.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p093_1.png

d3fe7ceb-7cb2-5d2d-a687-d1a4769a66c9.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images > OS Image Status
An OS Image can have the following statuses:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The OS Image has been created by the PCA but has not yet been activated by the MCA. |
| Enabled | The OS Image has been activated and is available for use within the platform. |
| Disabled | The OS Image has been disabled by the MCA and is no longer available for new deployments. |
d3fe7ceb-7cb2-5d2d-a687-d1a4769a66c9.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images > OS Image Status

ce8d889d-f0ff-5f1a-93c1-cf93d7e8f3d1.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images > Activating or Disabling an OS Image
To activate an OS Image in Pending or Disabled status, select the required image, open the Action menu, and click Activate.

During activation, the MCA must specify the Tenancy of the OS Image:

SHARED makes the OS Image available across subscriptions.

DEDICATED restricts the OS Image to selected subscriptions. When DEDICATED is selected, use + Subscription to select the required Organization and Subscription. Multiple subscriptions can be added where required.

Click Submit to complete the activation.

To disable an enabled OS Image, select the required image, open the Action menu, and click Disable.

Viewing OS Image Details
To view additional information for an OS Image, click the OS Image name.

The OS Image Details page displays information including the image name, UUID, provider, distribution, OS version, type, Kubernetes cluster usage indicator, status, creation and update timestamps, and the associated Zone.
ce8d889d-f0ff-5f1a-93c1-cf93d7e8f3d1.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > OS Images > Activating or Disabling an OS Image
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p094_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p094_2.png

f98cce64-61ab-5109-913b-f041f9dacf22.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers
The Servers page provides the MCA with visibility and lifecycle management of bare metal servers onboarded by the Private Cloud Admin (PCA).

Servers initially become visible to the MCA in Pending status after the PCA has completed the onboarding and activation process. The MCA must then activate the server before it can be made available for tenant use.

The page displays information including the Server Name, Client Server Name, Server Size, Organization, Subscription, Tenancy, Region, Zone, Status, Power Status, Subnet, and IP Address.
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p095_1.png

c186e7a7-0a4c-5f18-883d-85410f5f0634.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Status
A server can have the following main statuses:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The server has been activated by the PCA but has not yet been activated by the MCA. |
| Ready | The server has been activated by the MCA and is available for allocation to a tenant. |
| Allocated | The server has been allocated to a tenant, but an operating system has not yet been deployed. |
| Deployed | The server has been allocated to a tenant and an operating system has been deployed. |
c186e7a7-0a4c-5f18-883d-85410f5f0634.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Server Status

7e8a1acd-d4d2-5b37-a22e-55110afcd7a7.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Activating a Server
To activate a server in Pending status, select the required server, open the Action menu, and click Activate.

During activation, select the required Tenancy:

SHARED makes the server available for allocation across subscriptions.

DEDICATED restricts the server to the selected tenant subscription.

Click Activate to complete the activation. Once activated, the server transitions from Pending to Ready and becomes available for allocation.

A server can also be deactivated through the Action menu when its current state permits this. Allocated and Deployed servers cannot be deactivated.
7e8a1acd-d4d2-5b37-a22e-55110afcd7a7.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Activating a Server
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p096_1.png

882ce493-a6a0-56da-8666-baeefbe81bb1.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Viewing Server Details
To view additional information, click the Server Name.

The Server Details page provides the server configuration and allocation information, including its provider, region, zone, organization, subscription, tenancy, server size, operating system, power status, subnet, IP address, and current status.

Additional information is available through the tabs at the bottom of the Server Details page.

Network Interfaces displays the physical and configured network interfaces associated with the server.

Storage displays the storage devices discovered on the server.

Devices displays additional hardware device information discovered during server onboarding.

Security displays the access information associated with the deployed server, including the username, SSH key name, and key fingerprint.

For a Dedicated server, the Tenants tab also identifies the Organization and Subscription to which the server has been assigned.
882ce493-a6a0-56da-8666-baeefbe81bb1.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > BMaaS > Servers > Viewing Server Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p097_1.png

6cf270a6-ea99-5608-817c-c6e63e64de22.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration
The Administration section provides the MCA with controls for managing tenant resource policies and reviewing policy change requests. These controls define the resource limits available to individual subscriptions and provide visibility into requests to modify those limits.

5048bb9e-1fea-5443-9cde-41da8eb1ae8c.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies
Instance Policies define the maximum resource limits available to a subscription for a particular provider. The MCA can use this page to review the limits assigned to each Organization and Subscription and monitor current resource consumption against those limits.

The Instance Policies page displays the Organization, Subscription Name, Provider and configured limits for Nodes, vCPU, Memory, Storage and Elastic IPs. The available filter and search options can be used to locate specific policies.

To view a policy, select the required entry, open the Action menu and click View More.
5048bb9e-1fea-5443-9cde-41da8eb1ae8c.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p098_1.png

58cc1e41-43a6-5a15-bde6-5bf4f32a2fbd.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies > Viewing an Instance Policy
The Instance Policy page provides a detailed view of the resource limits and current consumption for the selected subscription and provider.

For each resource, the page displays the configured Threshold, the amount currently Used, and the Remaining capacity. Resources shown include Memory, Volume Storage, Virtual Machines, vCPU and Elastic IPs.

The Request History section displays previous requests associated with the policy, including the Request ID, Organization, Subscription, Requester, submission and update times, and request status. This provides the MCA with a historical view of requests that have affected the subscription's resource limits.
58cc1e41-43a6-5a15-bde6-5bf4f32a2fbd.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies > Viewing an Instance Policy
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p099_1.png

aaa39247-56e0-5814-ab11-d40f31430bf8.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Policy Requests
Policy Requests allows the MCA to review and action requests raised by Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP) users to modify the resource limits assigned to their subscription. Requests are associated with a specific Organization, Subscription and Provider.

The Policy Requests page displays the Request ID, Organization, Subscription Name, Provider, submission and update times, and the current status of each request. Requests may be filtered by Organization and Subscription, or located using the search function.
aaa39247-56e0-5814-ab11-d40f31430bf8.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Policy Requests

7443b186-019d-5f8c-b2fe-bf67c0efd5e2.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Policy Requests
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Pending | The request has been submitted by a CTP user and is awaiting review and action by the MCA. |
| Approved | The requested resource limit changes have been approved by the MCA. |
| Rejected | The requested resource limit changes have been rejected by the MCA. |

To view a request, click the Request ID directly. Alternatively, select the required request, open the Action menu and click View More.
7443b186-019d-5f8c-b2fe-bf67c0efd5e2.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Policy Requests
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p099_2.png

df409889-127a-5713-8e29-155da62ecb15.text:
Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Policy Requests > Reviewing a Policy Request
The Instance Policy Request window displays the request details, including the Request ID, Requester, Organization, Subscription, Provider, submission and update times, and current status. The Requester field identifies the CTP user who submitted the request.

The Resource Limit section compares the Original Threshold with the Requested Threshold for each applicable resource, including Memory, Volume Storage, Elastic IPs, vCPU and Virtual Machines. This allows the MCA to identify the requested changes before taking action.

For a Pending request, the MCA can enter a message where required and select Approve or Reject. Selecting Cancel closes the request without taking any action.

Once a request has been actioned, its status is updated to Approved or Rejected. The request remains available for review through the Request ID or View More, where the MCA can view the request details, the action taken and any associated comments.
df409889-127a-5713-8e29-155da62ecb15.section_path: Multi Cloud Administrator > Administration > Policy Requests > Reviewing a Policy Request
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p100_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p101_1.png

52e9b207-850b-5dd3-8f19-af405c652d40.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator
The Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP) provides tenant users with access to provision, configure, and manage cloud resources made available through Paragon. It provides a self-service interface for consuming the infrastructure and services that have been configured and enabled by the Private Cloud Administrator and Multi-Cloud Administrator.

Through the CTP, users can provision and manage Compute Nodes, Kubernetes clusters, networking resources, storage, connectivity, and Bare Metal servers. The portal also provides supporting services for SSH access, notifications, transaction tracking, resource organization, and management of subscription resource limits.

Resources within the CTP are managed within the context of the selected subscription. The availability of infrastructure, services, regions, zones, resource sizes, operating system images, and other platform resources depends on what has been configured and made available to that subscription through the administrative layers of Paragon.

This section describes the features available to a Cloud Tenant Portal user and the procedures for provisioning and managing resources throughout their lifecycle.

638b60a7-9929-504a-bbb0-3fa61b4986ea.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Dashboard
The Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP) Dashboard provides an overview of the cloud resources available within the selected subscription. It gives users a consolidated view of resource usage and status, together with recent activity performed within the subscription.

The summary cards at the top of the Dashboard display the total number of Virtual Machines, Volumes, Subnets, and Elastic IPs associated with the selected subscription.

The Dashboard provides additional status information for key resources. Virtual Machines are grouped by operational state, while Volumes, Subnets, and Elastic IPs show their current availability and usage. Additional summary panels provide information for Backups, Snapshots, Node Connects, and NAT Gateways.

The Recent Transactions section displays the latest operations performed within the subscription. Each entry includes the transaction ID, operation details, transaction status, user who initiated the operation, and the last updated time.

The Dashboard information reflects the currently selected subscription. Users can change the active subscription using the subscription selector at the top of the portal.

27d98553-f6ea-5eb2-b595-bac2bea48b27.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute
The Compute section allows Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP) users to create and manage virtual machine compute nodes within the selected subscription. From this section, users can provision new nodes, view existing nodes, manage node lifecycle operations, modify selected node settings, and review the resources associated with individual nodes.

9be83d12-8f24-5db0-90af-bde765727e57.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Nodes
The Nodes page displays the compute nodes available within the selected subscription. Each node entry provides information including the node name, node size, private and Elastic IP addresses, Resource Group, GPU configuration, Zone, Region, Provider, and current status.

c8749d39-6d48-5cb1-9762-4be570970b05.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Nodes
Deleted nodes are removed from the Nodes list and are no longer displayed.

To perform an operation on an existing node, select the node and open the Action menu. Depending on the current state of the node, available operations include Edit, Delete, View More, Start Node, Stop Node, and Resize Node.

Selecting View More, or clicking the node name directly, opens the Compute Node details page. This page displays the node configuration and provides additional information through the Network Interfaces, Storage, Security, History, and Monitoring tabs.

The Network Interfaces tab displays the primary network interface and any additional interfaces attached to the node. Additional network interfaces can be created and attached by selecting an available subnet and providing a display name for the interface. Existing additional interfaces can also be detached where applicable.

The Storage tab displays the root volume and any additional block volumes attached to the node. Additional volumes can be detached from the node, while the root volume remains associated with the node.

The Security tab displays the access information associated with the node, including the username, SSH access key name, and key fingerprint.

The History tab provides a record of operations performed on the node, such as creation, start, stop, resize, and other node lifecycle activities.

The Monitoring tab provides resource usage information for the node, including CPU usage, memory usage, network bandwidth, and storage activity. Monitoring data can be viewed for the available time period and exported using the Generate option. The timespan is from 5m (default) to 24 hours (maximum).

Node Operations

Start / Stop a Node
A running node can be stopped by selecting the node and choosing Action > Stop Node. A confirmation message is displayed before the operation is submitted. Once stopped, the corresponding Start Node operation becomes available.

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Resize a Node
The Resize Node operation allows the user to change the node to another available Node Size. During the resize operation, the node is unavailable.

Before confirming a resize, note that snapshots associated with the node are permanently deleted and existing backups cannot be restored to the resized node. The required Node Size should therefore be selected only after considering the impact shown in the confirmation screen.

592ee9d3-0210-5bd7-9725-6ddb5908911a.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Nodes > Deleting a Node
To delete a node, select the node and choose Action > Delete, or use the Delete option from the Compute Node details page. A confirmation screen displays the name and UUID of the selected node before the deletion is submitted.

The confirmation screen also provides the options Detach additional volume and Delete additional volume. These options are displayed as part of the node deletion process regardless of whether additional volumes are currently attached to the node. Where additional volumes are attached, select whether they should be detached and retained or deleted together with the node.

Creating a Compute Node

To create a new compute node, select Create from the Nodes page. The Create Compute Node wizard guides the user through five stages: Resource, Network, Instance, Node, and Review.

In the Resource stage, select the Provider, Region, Zone, and Resource Group within which the node will be provisioned.

In the Network stage, select the subnet to which the node will be connected. If a suitable subnet does not already exist, the Create Subnet option can be used to initiate creation of a new subnet.

In the Instance stage, select the required Node Size. The Node Size determines the compute configuration assigned to the new node.

In the Node stage, configure the operating system and access settings for the node. A new node can be created using an available Operating System image.

Alternatively, enable Create from existing backup image and select an available VM Backup Image to provision the node from a backup.

Provide the display name, hostname, username, and SSH access key. An existing access key can be selected, or a new access key can be created using Create Access Key.

Provide the display name, hostname, username, and SSH access key. An existing access key can be selected, or a new access key can be created using Create Access Key.

The root volume is created automatically from the selected Operating System image. The size of the root disk is defined by the OS Image and cannot be changed independently during Compute Node creation.

The user must select the Volume Type used for the root volume; however, selecting a Volume Type does not change the root disk capacity defined by the OS Image.

If a different root disk size is required, the appropriate OS Image must first be made available through Paragon. Customers should work with Singtel to define the required OS Image and root disk configuration.

Additional block volumes can be added during node creation using Add Volume. For each additional volume, specify the volume name, size, and volume type.

The Review stage displays the selected Resource, Network, Instance Type, Node, access, operating system, and volume settings. Review the configuration before submitting the request to create the compute node.

The page displays the Cluster Name, Kubernetes Version, Region, Resource Group, creation date, and current Status of each cluster. Use the Search field to locate a specific cluster, Kubernetes version, or Status.

The following cluster statuses may be displayed:

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters
Adding Worker Node and Deleting Worker Node are transient statuses displayed while the corresponding operation is in progress.

Note: If Kubernetes cluster creation or deletion fails, the operation cannot be retried directly from the Cloud Tenant Portal. Contact the Multi Cloud Administrator (MCA), who can review the failed workflow and retrigger the failed operation where required.

Managing a Kubernetes Cluster

Select a Kubernetes cluster and open the Action menu to access the available cluster operations:

Download Configuration downloads the Kubernetes configuration file for the selected cluster. The configuration file can be used by a Kubernetes client to connect to and manage the cluster.

Add Worker Node allows additional worker nodes to be added to an existing cluster.

Delete permanently deletes the selected Kubernetes cluster.

View More opens the Kubernetes Cluster Details page and displays additional information about the cluster and its worker nodes.

Note: All operations may not be available for nodes in transient or failed states.

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Adding Worker Nodes
Additional worker nodes can be added to an active Kubernetes cluster.

Select the cluster, open the Action menu, and select Add Worker Node. The Add Worker page displays the existing worker node groups, including the group name, type, size, and current number of worker nodes.

For the required worker group, specify the number of Additional Worker Nodes to be added and select Submit.

The resulting number of workers is calculated as the current worker count plus the number of additional workers specified.

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Viewing Kubernetes Cluster Details
Click the Cluster Name, or select the cluster and use Action > View More, to open the Kubernetes Cluster Details page.

The page displays information including the Cluster Name, UUID, Cluster Endpoint, Kubernetes Version, Provider, Region, Zone, Resource Group, creation date, creator, and current Status.

The Worker Node tab displays the worker groups configured for the cluster. Expand a worker group to view its individual worker nodes, including the node name, UUID, role, and status.

Worker nodes can also be deleted individually from this page by selecting the delete icon for the required active worker node. Individual worker node deletion is performed from the Kubernetes Cluster Details page.

The History tab provides a record of cluster operations, such as cluster creation and the addition or deletion of worker nodes. Each entry displays the transaction ID, start and end times, status, user, and linked resources associated with the operation.

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Deleting a Kubernetes Cluster
To delete a cluster, select the required cluster, open the Action menu, and select Delete.

A confirmation window displays the name and UUID of the selected cluster. Review the information carefully before proceeding. Cluster deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

Select Delete to confirm the operation or Cancel to return without deleting the cluster.

Creating a Kubernetes Cluster

Select Create from the Kubernetes Clusters page to start the Create Kubernetes Cluster wizard. Cluster creation is completed through four stages: Basic Information, Control Plane, Worker Nodes, and Review.

Step 1: Basic Information
Enter the Cluster Name, then select the Provider, Region, Zone, Resource Group, and Kubernetes Version to be used for the cluster.

The available options are determined by the resources and services available to the current subscription.

Select Next to continue.

Step 2: Control Plane
Select the required Size for the control-plane nodes and the Number of Master Nodes.

The available master node counts are 1, 3, or 5.

Select Next to continue.
b5f69495-7811-5ea5-ade2-24e5afbca41d.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Compute > Kubernetes Clusters > Deleting a Kubernetes Cluster

61a05431-1fcc-5855-b6f7-809dcec25d84.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network
The Network section provides the networking resources and controls required to connect and manage workloads within the Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP). These resources define how Compute Nodes and Bare Metal servers are connected to internal networks, communicate between networks, and access external networks.

Networking within CTP is built from several related components. Subnets provide the underlying network address space for resources, while Network Interfaces connect individual resources to those subnets. Elastic IPs provide externally routable addresses that can be used by services such as Node Connect, NAT Gateways, and outbound routes.

NAT Gateways provide outbound connectivity from private subnets, while Route Tables control the paths available between networks and external destinations. Network Policies provide traffic control by defining the inbound and outbound communication that is permitted for Subnets and Elastic IPs.

f75f2446-4e8e-5896-8035-4644bf6f75ee.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets
Subnets provide the network address ranges used when provisioning compute resources in Paragon. At least one available subnet is required in the target Zone before a Virtual Machine or Bare Metal server can be provisioned.

Subnet address ranges are allocated by the platform based on availability and cannot be selected by the user. A newly created subscription does not have any subnets available by default, and a subnet must therefore be created before resources can be provisioned.

The Subnets page displays the subnets available to the current subscription, including the subnet name, IPv4 CIDR, current usage, Resource Group, Region, Zone, Provider, and status.
f75f2446-4e8e-5896-8035-4644bf6f75ee.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets

Delete subnet

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets > View More
Select the subnet name directly, or select the subnet and choose Action > View More, to open the Subnet Details page. This page displays the subnet UUID, name, IPv4 CIDR, current usage, Zone, Region, Resource Group, status, and creation and update timestamps.

The Usage tab displays resources currently using IP addresses from the subnet. The Route Table tab allows additional routes associated with the subnet to be managed, while the History tab provides the activity history for the subnet.

Managing Subnet Routes
From the Subnet Details page, select the Route Table tab to view and manage routes associated with the subnet. Select Add to create a new route.

Two route types can be configured:

5478ed41-b6cd-5645-9709-82ff659052e7.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets > Managing Subnet Routes
Two route types can be configured:
| Route Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Internal | Creates a route to another internal subnet within the same subscription. |
| Outbound | Creates a route to an external network using an Elastic IP as the next hop. |
5478ed41-b6cd-5645-9709-82ff659052e7.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets > Managing Subnet Routes

5ef9ffe4-ea55-5e5d-b3fe-44745e239f99.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets > Managing Subnet Routes
A corresponding reverse route is created automatically.

For an Internal route, select the destination subnet and select Add.

For an Outbound route, select the Elastic IP to be used as the Next Hop (Via), enter the destination IP address or subnet, and select Add.

Creating a route does not by itself permit traffic between the connected networks. Paragon uses an implicit-deny network policy model, and the appropriate Network Policies must also be configured to allow the required communication.

Existing routes can be selected and deleted from the Route Table tab when they are no longer required.

Creating a Subnet

To create a subnet, select Create from the Subnets page.

Select the Provider, Region, and Zone in which the subnet will be created. Select the required Subnet Type, either Virtual Machine or Bare Metal, followed by the Virtual Network and Resource Group. Enter a name for the subnet and select Submit.

The subnet address range is assigned automatically by the platform based on the available address space. The user does not specify the CIDR range during subnet creation.

Once the subnet becomes Active, it is available for use when provisioning resources within the corresponding Zone.
5ef9ffe4-ea55-5e5d-b3fe-44745e239f99.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Subnets > Managing Subnet Routes

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Interfaces
A Network Interface provides network connectivity for a Compute Node. Every Compute Node is created with a primary network interface, with a private IP address allocated from the subnet selected during node creation.

Additional Network Interfaces can be created and attached to a Compute Node using other available subnets within the same Zone. This allows a node to connect to multiple subnets where required.

The Network Interfaces page displays the interface Name, IP Address, attached node, whether the interface is the primary interface, Subnet, Elastic IP, Region, Zone, Provider, and current Status.

The following statuses may be displayed:
32176295-ca3d-5615-a2ce-d674cf30e695.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Interfaces
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p126_1.png

4c7748bd-f236-57fd-967c-418b16e0b09c.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Interfaces
The following statuses may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Attached | The Network Interface is currently attached to a Compute Node. The primary Network Interface created with a node is always attached. |
| Available | The Network Interface is not currently attached and is available to be attached to a Compute Node. |

Use the Search field to locate a Network Interface. Select a Network Interface to access the available actions.

The available actions depend on the current state of the Network Interface. These include Edit, Delete, View More, Attach, and Detach.

Managing a Network Interface

Click the Network Interface name, or select the Network Interface and choose Action > View More, to open the Network Interface details page.

The details page displays information including the Network Interface name and UUID, private and Elastic IP addresses, Provider, MAC address, Subnet, Zone, Region, current state, and creation and update timestamps.

The History section displays transactions associated with the Network Interface, including operations such as creation, attachment, and detachment.

Editing a Network Interface
To change the display name of a Network Interface, select the interface and choose Action > Edit. Enter the new name and click Submit.

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Interfaces > Attaching a Network Interface
An Available Network Interface can be attached to an eligible Compute Node.

Select the Network Interface and choose Action > Attach, or click Attach from the Network Interface details page. Select an available node and click Submit.

During the attachment process, the node may undergo multiple start and stop cycles while the network configuration is applied. Once the operation is complete, the Network Interface is shown as Attached.

An attached additional Network Interface can subsequently be detached from the node using the Detach action.

e312fce9-0724-5e84-be36-37ef1bddb4f6.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Interfaces > Deleting a Network Interface
To permanently remove a Network Interface, select it and choose Action > Delete, or click Delete from the Network Interface details page.

A confirmation window displays the Network Interface name and UUID. Review the selected Network Interface and click Delete to proceed, or Cancel to return without making changes.

Note: The default primary Network Interface and Network Interfaces that are currently attached to a Compute Node cannot be deleted. An additional Network Interface must first be detached from the node before it can be deleted.

Creating a Network Interface

Click Create from the Network Interfaces page to create an additional Network Interface.

Select the Provider, Region, Zone, and Subnet, then enter a name for the Network Interface.

A Compute Node can optionally be selected during creation. If a node is selected, the new Network Interface is created and attached to that node. If no node is selected, the Network Interface is created in the Available state and can be attached later.

Click Submit to create the Network Interface.
e312fce9-0724-5e84-be36-37ef1bddb4f6.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Interfaces > Deleting a Network Interface
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p128_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p129_1.png

d670438d-98cf-5f23-8f0c-c22ab9a1cf42.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs
Elastic IPs are static IPv4 addresses that can be allocated for use with resources that require connectivity to external networks. Depending on the service offering, an Elastic IP may provide public Internet connectivity or connectivity to a restricted external network.

Elastic IPs are associated with a specific provider and zone and can only be used with compatible resources within the same provider and zone. Elastic IPs cannot be moved between zones.

The Elastic IPs page displays the Elastic IPs allocated to the current subscription, including the IP address, assigned resource, assignment type, resource group, region, zone, provider, and current status.
d670438d-98cf-5f23-8f0c-c22ab9a1cf42.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p130_1.png

6b420ca4-7762-5438-98a0-e8e363529cbd.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Available | The Elastic IP is allocated to the subscription and is available for use. |
| Assigned | The Elastic IP is currently assigned to a resource. |
6b420ca4-7762-5438-98a0-e8e363529cbd.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs

49f9f7d4-794f-5672-b688-76aef8324386.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs
The Assignment Type identifies how an assigned Elastic IP is being used. For example, an Elastic IP may be assigned to a Node Connect, NAT Gateway, or outbound route.

Use the Search field to locate an Elastic IP. Select an Elastic IP to access the available actions.

The available actions depend on the current state of the Elastic IP. These include Edit, Release, and View More.

Managing an Elastic IP

Edit an Elastic IP
To edit an Elastic IP, select the Elastic IP and choose Edit from the Action menu.

The Elastic IP name can be updated. Enter the new name and click Submit to save the change.
49f9f7d4-794f-5672-b688-76aef8324386.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p126_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p131_2.png

ba4dbfe9-c380-5dd9-9cef-ab480f352df5.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs > View Elastic IP Details
Click the Elastic IP name to open its details directly. Alternatively, select the Elastic IP and choose View More from the Action menu.

The Elastic IP Details page displays information including the UUID, name, IP address, provider, region, zone, resource group, status, and creation and update timestamps.

The History section displays transactions associated with the Elastic IP, including the transaction description, transaction ID, start and end times, status, user, and linked resources. This can be used to review operations involving the Elastic IP and its associated resources.
ba4dbfe9-c380-5dd9-9cef-ab480f352df5.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs > View Elastic IP Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p132_1.png

0ae72228-e928-50f7-b32b-cfc17a1481c9.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs > Release an Elastic IP
An Elastic IP that is no longer required can be returned by selecting the Elastic IP and choosing Release from the Action menu. Review the confirmation message and click Release to proceed.

An Elastic IP cannot be released while it is assigned to another resource. The associated resource or configuration, such as a Node Connect, NAT Gateway, or outbound route, must first be removed before the Elastic IP can be released.

Allocate an Elastic IP

To allocate a new Elastic IP, click Allocate from the Elastic IPs page.

Select the Provider, Region, Zone, Resource Group, and Elastic Pool, and enter a name for the Elastic IP. Click Submit to allocate the Elastic IP.

The IP address is automatically allocated from the selected Elastic Pool. The specific IP address cannot be selected during allocation.

Once successfully allocated, the Elastic IP is shown with an Available status and can be used by a compatible resource in the same provider and zone.
0ae72228-e928-50f7-b32b-cfc17a1481c9.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Elastic IPs > Release an Elastic IP
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p132_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p133_1.png

cb90bb66-2752-575f-a853-3a676ac52b28.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > NAT Gateways
NAT Gateways provide outbound connectivity from resources within a subnet to networks outside the zone. Traffic routed through the NAT Gateway uses the Elastic IP associated with the gateway as its source IP.

A NAT Gateway provides outbound connectivity only. External services cannot use the NAT Gateway to initiate connections directly to the private subnet or node IP addresses.

The NAT Gateways page displays the NAT Gateways available within the current subscription. The page shows the NAT Gateway name, associated Elastic IP, attached subnet, region, zone, provider, and current status.

Use the Search field to locate a NAT Gateway by name or status.

Select a NAT Gateway to make the available options accessible from the Action menu. From here, the NAT Gateway can be edited, deleted, or opened using View More.

Manage NAT Gateways
cb90bb66-2752-575f-a853-3a676ac52b28.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > NAT Gateways
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p134_1.png

3cdc3465-35e1-52ad-8cf3-af64d26ce22b.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > NAT Gateways > View NAT Gateway Details
Click the NAT Gateway name to open the NAT Gateway Details page directly. Alternatively, select the NAT Gateway and select Action > View More.

The details page displays the NAT Gateway name and UUID, associated Elastic IP, attached subnet, provider, region, zone, current status, and creation and modification timestamps.

Edit a NAT Gateway
Select the required NAT Gateway and select Action > Edit. Update the NAT Gateway name and click Submit to save the change.
3cdc3465-35e1-52ad-8cf3-af64d26ce22b.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > NAT Gateways > View NAT Gateway Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p135_1.png
