5b712f32-aa64-552f-9f64-3650fa343920.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > NAT Gateways > Delete a NAT Gateway
Select the required NAT Gateway and select Action > Delete. The confirmation window displays the name and UUID of the selected NAT Gateway and warns that the deletion is permanent.

Click Delete to confirm the operation or Cancel to return without making changes.

Create a NAT Gateway

Click Create from the NAT Gateways page to create a new NAT Gateway.

Select the Provider, Region, and Zone, followed by an available Elastic IP and the Subnet to which the NAT Gateway will be attached. Enter a name for the NAT Gateway and click Submit to create it.

If an Elastic IP has not already been allocated, click Allocate Elastic IP to allocate one before continuing.

A NAT Gateway is associated with a specific subnet, and each subnet can have only one NAT Gateway.

Depending on the selected provider, outbound traffic from a newly created NAT Gateway may be blocked by default. Where required, configure and apply the appropriate Network Policies to enable the required external communication.
5b712f32-aa64-552f-9f64-3650fa343920.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > NAT Gateways > Delete a NAT Gateway
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p136_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p137_1.png

24f22b74-01c7-5e9b-b0db-1ef7f7f96e42.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables
Route Tables define the routes used to provide connectivity between a network resource and other networks or resources. A Route Table is created automatically for the associated network resource and does not need to be created separately by the user.

Routes are local to the Route Table and the network resource to which it is attached, allowing routing to be managed independently for each network.

Manage Route Tables

The Route Tables page displays the Route Tables available within the current subscription. The page shows the Route Table name, attached network resource, region, zone, provider, and current status.

Use the Search field to locate a specific Route Table.

Select a Route Table to make the available options accessible from the Action menu. From here, the Route Table name can be edited or the Route Table can be opened using View More.

Route Tables are created automatically with their associated network resources and cannot be manually created or deleted from this page.
24f22b74-01c7-5e9b-b0db-1ef7f7f96e42.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p138_1.png

9225b00c-02c0-5bb5-b3bd-f67ae342f2fd.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables > View Route Table Details
Click the Route Table name to open the Route Table Details page directly. Alternatively, select the Route Table and select Action > View More.

The details page displays information including the Route Table UUID, name, attached network resource, provider, region, zone, state, and creation and update timestamps.

The Route section displays the routes configured for the Route Table, including the route type, next hop where applicable, destination, and status.

Add a Route
From the Route Table Details page, click Add to add a route to the Route Table.

Routes can be configured as Internal or Outbound:
9225b00c-02c0-5bb5-b3bd-f67ae342f2fd.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables > View Route Table Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p139_1.png

9e55f72e-d1cb-5281-bd57-bb25135f361f.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables > Add a Route
Routes can be configured as Internal or Outbound:
| Route Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Internal | Creates a route to another internal subnet within the same subscription. |
| Outbound | Creates a route to an external destination using an Elastic IP as the next hop. |
9e55f72e-d1cb-5281-bd57-bb25135f361f.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables > Add a Route

05dc10a3-de42-535f-b131-9cb724a8db73.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables > Add a Route
For an Internal route, select the destination subnet. Creating the route establishes the routing path between the subnets, but the appropriate Network Policies must also be configured to permit traffic between them.

For an Outbound route, select the Elastic IP to use as the next hop and specify the destination IP address or subnet. The corresponding reverse route is created automatically. The appropriate Network Policies must still be configured to permit the required traffic.

Remove a Route
Routes can also be removed from the Route Table Details page. Select the required route and click Remove to delete it from the Route Table.
05dc10a3-de42-535f-b131-9cb724a8db73.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Route Tables > Add a Route

a2a0d10e-500d-5cc1-ba4f-5e2f53875a84.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies
Network Policies control inbound and outbound traffic for network resources by defining rules based on protocol, source and destination addresses, ports, and rule actions. Policies can be assigned to an Elastic IP or a subnet, allowing traffic controls to be applied at the appropriate network boundary.

A Network Policy may contain multiple inbound and outbound rules. Rules are evaluated according to their configured priority, with the lowest priority number evaluated first.

For policies assigned to a subnet, the policy controls traffic for the nodes using that subnet. For policies assigned to an Elastic IP, the applicable rule direction depends on how the Elastic IP is being used. An Elastic IP used for Node Connect requires inbound rules, while a a NAT Gateway requires outbound rules on a subnet network policy.

Only one Network Policy can be assigned to an individual Elastic IP or subnet.

Manage Network Policies

The Network Policies page displays the policies available within the current subscription. The page shows the policy name, type, assigned resource, region, zone, provider, and current status.

Use the Search field to locate a Network Policy.

Select a Network Policy to access the available options from the Action menu.

From the Action menu, you can Edit, Delete or View More.
a2a0d10e-500d-5cc1-ba4f-5e2f53875a84.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p140_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p140_2.png

89d9b51a-1097-54e0-8da8-aff470c3ae56.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > Edit a Network Policy Name
From the Network Policies page, select the required policy and select Action > Edit.

Enter the updated policy name and submit the change.

The Edit option available directly from the Network Policies page changes only the policy name. To modify the rules contained within a policy, open the policy using View More and use the Edit option from the Network Policy Details page.
89d9b51a-1097-54e0-8da8-aff470c3ae56.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > Edit a Network Policy Name
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p141_1.png

f397da0b-2ebd-5647-9735-3d521469465d.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > Delete a Network Policy
From the Network Policies page, select the required policy and select Action > Delete.

A confirmation dialog displays the name and UUID of the selected Network Policy. Review the information and click Delete to confirm.

Deleting a Network Policy removes the traffic rules applied by that policy from the associated resource.
f397da0b-2ebd-5647-9735-3d521469465d.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > Delete a Network Policy
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p141_2.png

dabeff1c-c6b5-5377-b795-42c64947ae2c.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > View Network Policy Details
Click the Network Policy name to open the Network Policy Details page directly. Alternatively, select the policy and select Action > View More.

The details page displays information including the policy name, UUID, type, assigned resource, provider, region, zone, status, and creation and modification timestamps.

The Inbound Rule and Outbound Rule tabs display the rules configured for each traffic direction. Each rule shows its priority, action, protocol, source address and port, and destination address and port.
dabeff1c-c6b5-5377-b795-42c64947ae2c.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > View Network Policy Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p142_1.png

fcec6f99-ab15-5b4e-9dbe-7f1449f30904.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > Edit Network Policy Rules
From the Network Policy Details page, click Edit to open the Update Network Policy page.

Unlike the Edit option on the main Network Policies page, this page allows the rules contained within the policy to be managed. Existing rules can be edited or removed, and additional inbound or outbound rules can be added.

Rules can also be reordered by dragging them to the required position. The lowest numbered rule has the highest priority. After making the required changes, click Submit to update the Network Policy.
fcec6f99-ab15-5b4e-9dbe-7f1449f30904.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Network Policies > Edit Network Policy Rules
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p142_2.png

e2825a02-01f8-5c1c-a37c-4707ab3fad83.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Create a Network Policy
From the Network Policies page, click Create.

Enter a name and select the Provider, Region, and Zone. Select the required Policy Type and the resource to which the policy will be assigned.

The supported policy types are:
e2825a02-01f8-5c1c-a37c-4707ab3fad83.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Create a Network Policy
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p143_1.png

28b8ecdd-4316-5d05-8241-df7748fa9e76.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Create a Network Policy
The supported policy types are:
| Policy Type | Description |
|---|---|
| ELASTIC IP | Applies the Network Policy to a selected Elastic IP. |
| _ SUBNET | Applies the Network Policy to a selected subnet. |

The Assignment field displays the resources available for the selected policy type.

Only one Network Policy can be assigned to an individual Elastic IP or subnet.
28b8ecdd-4316-5d05-8241-df7748fa9e76.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Create a Network Policy

b6408aca-cd11-52f8-89fd-d9e935446591.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Create a Network Policy > Configure Rules
Use the Inbound Rule and Outbound Rule tabs to configure the traffic permitted or denied by the policy. Click Add Rule under the appropriate tab to create a rule.

For each rule, configure the required action, protocol, source information, and destination information.

The available rule actions are Accept, Reject, and Drop. Supported protocol selections include ALL, TCP, UDP, TCP & UDP, and ICMP.

Source and destination addresses and ports can then be specified according to the traffic that the rule is intended to control.

Important: When configuring rules for Compute Nodes or Bare Metal servers, use the resource's private IP address as the applicable node/server address. For example, when creating an inbound rule on an Elastic IP associated with a node, the destination is the node's private IP address rather than its Elastic IP address.

Once all required rules have been configured, review their order and click Submit to create the Network Policy.
b6408aca-cd11-52f8-89fd-d9e935446591.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Network > Create a Network Policy > Configure Rules
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p144_1.png

bd18e804-be16-5091-ba3c-a3f3cd73c9f3.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage
The Storage section enables Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP) users to manage storage resources available within their subscription. These resources provide persistent storage for Compute Nodes and support data protection and recovery operations.

The Storage section provides access to Block Volumes, Backups, and Snapshots. Block Volumes provide persistent storage that can be attached to Compute Nodes, while Backups and Snapshots provide options for preserving and recovering node and volume data.

fab3e961-77ef-5b0d-b49a-a7b843ee9b7e.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes
Block Volumes provide additional block storage that can be attached to Compute Nodes within Paragon. Block Volumes are provisioned from the shared storage resources made available through the platform and are associated with a specific Provider, Region, and Zone.

When a Block Volume is attached to a node, it is presented to the operating system as a raw, unformatted block device. Paragon does not automatically create partitions, create a filesystem, or mount the volume within the operating system.

The user is responsible for preparing the attached volume according to the requirements of the workload, including defining the required partition layout, selecting and creating the filesystem, and configuring the required mount point.

Note: This is the expected behaviour for additional Block Volumes. For example, an attached data volume may be visible within the operating system as a device such as /dev/sdb without any partitions, filesystem, or mount point until it is configured by the user.

The Block Volumes page displays the volumes available within the current subscription. The page shows the volume name, type, size, attached node where applicable, Resource Group, Zone, Provider, Region, and current status.

The following statuses may be displayed:
fab3e961-77ef-5b0d-b49a-a7b843ee9b7e.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes

3cc83998-f17e-57a5-bd6f-93bd008c43b1.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes
The following statuses may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Available | The Block Volume is not currently attached to a Compute Node and is available for use. |
| Attached | The Block Volume is currently attached to a Compute Node. |
3cc83998-f17e-57a5-bd6f-93bd008c43b1.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes

d7953b59-5969-5e35-b12b-9c85d8d2a4b6.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes
The root volumes associated with Compute Nodes are also displayed on the Block Volumes page.

Manage Block Volumes

Select a Block Volume to access the available options from the Action menu. Depending on the volume and its current state, the available actions include Edit, Delete, View More, Attach, and Detach.
d7953b59-5969-5e35-b12b-9c85d8d2a4b6.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p146_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p146_2.png

5094312d-7c3c-5b47-9ce6-0ffbcf6fa337.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > View Block Volume Details
Click the Block Volume name to open the Block Volume details page directly. Alternatively, select the required volume and choose Action > View More.

The details page displays information including the volume name and UUID, type, attached node where applicable, Resource Group, Provider, Region, Zone, current status, and creation and update timestamps.

The History section displays transactions associated with the Block Volume.

Edit a Block Volume
To change the name of a Block Volume, select the required volume and choose Action > Edit. Enter the new name and click Submit to save the change.
5094312d-7c3c-5b47-9ce6-0ffbcf6fa337.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > View Block Volume Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p147_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p147_2.png

287c72fc-8c73-50d8-855a-4e7786b557b2.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > Attach a Block Volume
An Available Block Volume can be attached to an eligible Compute Node.

Select the required volume and choose Action > Attach, or use the Attach option from the Block Volume details page. Select an available node and click Submit.

Once the operation is complete, the volume is associated with the selected node and its status changes to Attached.
287c72fc-8c73-50d8-855a-4e7786b557b2.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > Attach a Block Volume
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p148_1.png

4d3881f0-25e9-5a14-9607-91330b6fa700.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > Detach a Block Volume
An additional Block Volume that is currently attached to a Compute Node can be detached when it is no longer required by that node.

Select the attached volume and choose Action > Detach, or use the Detach option from the Block Volume details page. Review the volume information in the confirmation window and click Submit to detach it.

Once detached, the volume returns to the Available state and can subsequently be attached to another eligible Compute Node.

Note: Root volumes cannot be attached or detached using these operations.
4d3881f0-25e9-5a14-9607-91330b6fa700.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > Detach a Block Volume
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p148_2.png

711c405f-fa65-57b2-832b-036218043c76.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > Delete a Block Volume
An Available Block Volume can be permanently removed using Action > Delete.

Attached Block Volumes cannot be deleted. The volume must first be detached from its Compute Node before it can be deleted. Root volumes remain associated with their Compute Nodes and cannot be deleted independently through the Block Volumes page.

Create a Block Volume

Click Create from the Block Volumes page to create a new Block Volume.

Select the Provider, Region, Zone, Resource Group, and required Type. Enter the required volume Size in GB and provide a name for the Block Volume.

Click Submit to create the volume.

Once successfully created, the Block Volume is displayed with an Available status and can be attached to an eligible Compute Node.
711c405f-fa65-57b2-832b-036218043c76.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Block Volumes > Delete a Block Volume
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p149_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p150_1.png

c8d97a7d-3244-5f0f-a144-103abf4a8c5f.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups
Backups provide recoverable copies of Compute Nodes within Paragon and support recovery in the event that the original node is corrupted or lost. Unlike snapshots, backups are stored separately from the source node and can be restored independently.

The Backups page displays the backups available within the current subscription. The page shows the backup name, source Node, size, Zone, Provider, creation time, and current status.

Manage Backups

Select a backup to access the available options from the Action menu. Depending on the backup and its current state, the available actions include Edit, Delete, View More, and Restore.
c8d97a7d-3244-5f0f-a144-103abf4a8c5f.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p151_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p151_2.png

fe030cee-bc4f-527a-8245-79bdfcd922d4.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups > View Backup Details
Click the backup name to open the Backup details page directly. Alternatively, select the required backup and choose Action > View More.

The details page displays information including the backup name and UUID, Provider, Region, Zone, source Node, size, current status, and creation and update timestamps.

The History section displays transactions associated with the backup.

Edit a Backup
To change the name of a backup, select the required backup and choose Action > Edit. Enter the new name and click Submit to save the change.
fe030cee-bc4f-527a-8245-79bdfcd922d4.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups > View Backup Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p152_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p152_2.png

dc1b78b0-10e1-5ab1-9e76-43dce4c23798.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups > Restore a Backup
A successfully created backup can be used to restore the backed-up Compute Node.

Select the required backup and choose Action > Restore, or use the Restore option from the Backup details page.

During the restore process, new volumes are created for the restored node. Where applicable, provide new names for the volumes that will be created.

If additional non-root volumes are currently attached to the node, select whether these volumes should be detached for later use or deleted. Click Submit to begin the restore operation.
dc1b78b0-10e1-5ab1-9e76-43dce4c23798.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups > Restore a Backup
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p153_1.png

972b36e2-f240-598b-8b5e-48ec06667df2.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups > Delete a Backup
A backup can be permanently removed using Action > Delete, or the Delete option from the Backup details page.

Review the backup information displayed in the confirmation window and click Delete to permanently remove the backup.

Create a Backup

Click Create from the Backups page to create a new backup.

Select the Provider, Region, and Zone, then select the Node to be backed up. Select the required backup Mode and provide a name for the backup.

The available backup modes are Safe and Snapshot.

Click Submit to create the backup.

Once submitted, the backup is displayed with a Pending status while the operation is in progress. Once successfully created, the status changes to Created.

Note: The machine will be stopped and started during this process.
972b36e2-f240-598b-8b5e-48ec06667df2.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Backups > Delete a Backup

3b8366ad-7386-5622-a292-08cb4ca9eb35.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots
Snapshots preserve the state of a Compute Node at a specific point in time, allowing the node to be rolled back if required. They are typically used as a short-term recovery point before activities such as patching, upgrades, testing, or other changes where a quick rollback may be required.

A snapshot can optionally include the contents of the node's RAM. Including RAM preserves the in-memory state but increases the time required to create the snapshot.

Snapshots are closely associated with the configuration of the source node. Changes to the node configuration, such as adding a new disk, may invalidate existing snapshots and make them unavailable for rollback.

The Snapshots page displays the snapshots available within the current subscription. The page shows the snapshot name, source Node, Zone, Provider, whether RAM was included, and current status.

Manage Snapshots

Select a snapshot to access the available options from the Action menu. The available actions include Edit, Delete, View More, and Rollback.
3b8366ad-7386-5622-a292-08cb4ca9eb35.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p156_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p156_2.png

c325f06b-1108-58d7-826d-3c9538dda295.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > View Snapshot Details
Click the snapshot name to open the Snapshot details page directly. Alternatively, select the required snapshot and choose Action > View More.

The details page displays information including the snapshot name and UUID, source Node, Provider, Region, Zone, Resource Group, whether RAM was included, current status, last rollback information, and creation and update timestamps.

The History section displays transactions associated with the snapshot.

Edit a Snapshot
To change the name of a snapshot, select the required snapshot and choose Action > Edit. Enter the new name and click Submit to save the change.
c325f06b-1108-58d7-826d-3c9538dda295.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > View Snapshot Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p157_1.png

c60e65d9-c066-54aa-8a8e-3f1a019c6ce5.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > Rollback a Snapshot
A snapshot can be used to return its source Compute Node to the state captured when the snapshot was created.

Select the required snapshot and choose Action > Rollback, or use the Rollback option from the Snapshot details page. Review the snapshot information displayed in the confirmation window and click Confirm to begin the rollback.

Note: Rolling back changes the state of the source node to the point captured by the selected snapshot. Ensure that the correct snapshot has been selected before confirming the operation.
c60e65d9-c066-54aa-8a8e-3f1a019c6ce5.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > Rollback a Snapshot
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p158_1.png

a2448a45-bcc0-5d12-ae98-0801c2fcdad2.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > Delete a Snapshot
A snapshot can be permanently removed using Action > Delete, or the Delete option from the Snapshot details page.

Review the snapshot information displayed in the confirmation window and click Delete to permanently remove the snapshot.

Create a Snapshot

Click Create from the Snapshots page to create a new snapshot.

Select the Provider, Region, and Zone, then select the Node for which the snapshot will be created.

Select whether the contents of the node's RAM should be included in the snapshot using the RAM option:
a2448a45-bcc0-5d12-ae98-0801c2fcdad2.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > Delete a Snapshot
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p158_2.png

2cf2a996-0ce5-5932-b8d9-cea6e69f394f.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Storage > Snapshots > Delete a Snapshot
Select whether the contents of the node's RAM should be included in the snapshot using the RAM option:
| RAM | Description |
|---|---|
| No | Creates the snapshot without preserving the contents of RAM. |
| Yes | Includes the contents of RAM in the snapshot. Snapshot creation takes longer when this option is selected. |

Provide a name for the snapshot and click Submit.

Once successfully created, the snapshot is displayed with a Created status and is available for rollback.

f63a3c7e-dd56-5880-9ca9-fd632d3dba65.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect
The Connect section provides the functionality required to establish external connectivity to resources deployed within the Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP).

External connectivity is provided through Node Connect, which associates an Elastic IP with a network interface belonging to a Compute Node or Bare Metal server. The connection works together with the applicable Network Policies to control the traffic permitted to reach the resource.

3abce80a-ac55-5a76-aca7-45b67f81a327.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect > Node Connect
Node Connect provides external connectivity to a Compute Node or Bare Metal server by associating an Elastic IP with one of the resource's network interfaces. The Elastic IP must be available within the same Provider and Zone as the target resource.

Once assigned to a Node Connect, the Elastic IP is dedicated to that connection and is not available for use by other resources.

Creating a Node Connect does not by itself permit traffic to the resource. Paragon applies network access controls separately, and an appropriate Network Policy must be configured to allow the required inbound traffic.

The Node Connect page displays the connections available within the current subscription. The page shows the Node Connect name, Elastic IP, assigned network interface, Region, Zone, Provider, and current status.

Manage Node Connects

Select a Node Connect to access the available options from the Action menu. The available actions include Edit, Delete, and View More.
3abce80a-ac55-5a76-aca7-45b67f81a327.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect > Node Connect
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p160_1.png

f520afe6-8af2-501a-9e75-530a6730ab8a.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect > Node Connect > View Node Connect Details
Click the Node Connect name to open the Node Connect details page directly. Alternatively, select the required Node Connect and choose Action > View More.

The details page displays information including the Node Connect name and UUID, Elastic IP, associated VM or Bare Metal resource, Network Interface, Provider, Region, Zone, current status, and creation and update timestamps.

Edit a Node Connect
To change the name of a Node Connect, select the required connection and choose Action > Edit. Enter the new name and click Submit to save the change.
f520afe6-8af2-501a-9e75-530a6730ab8a.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect > Node Connect > View Node Connect Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p161_2.png

7bd998d8-e75d-568f-b699-26bc35be2732.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect > Node Connect > Delete a Node Connect
A Node Connect can be permanently removed when external connectivity through that connection is no longer required.

Select the required Node Connect and choose Action > Delete, or use the Delete option from the Node Connect details page. Review the connection information displayed in the confirmation window and click Delete.

Deleting the Node Connect removes the association between the Elastic IP and the resource. The Elastic IP can subsequently be used for another eligible resource or released if it is no longer required.

Create a Node Connect

Click Create from the Node Connect page to create a new connection.

Select the Provider, Region, and Zone, followed by the required Resource Type. Node Connect supports both Virtual Machine and Bare Metal resources.

Select the target Node and the Network Interface to which the connection will be associated. Select an available Elastic IP from the same Provider and Zone. If an Elastic IP has not already been allocated, use Allocate Elastic IP to allocate one.

Provide a name for the Node Connect and click Submit.

Once successfully created, the Node Connect is displayed with an Active status.
7bd998d8-e75d-568f-b699-26bc35be2732.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Connect > Node Connect > Delete a Node Connect

619d9941-7c13-5104-9429-8794903578ba.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services
The Services section provides access to supporting functions used to manage access credentials, platform notifications, and operational activity within the Cloud Tenant Portal (CTP).

These services complement the compute, network, and storage resources managed through CTP and provide users with the supporting information and configuration required for day-today resource management.

a4594669-97dd-5f9e-a5fe-a1c5734f64bc.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > SSH Keys
SSH Keys provide a secure method of authenticating access to Compute Nodes without using password-based authentication. Users can register their SSH public keys in CTP and select an available key when provisioning a Compute Node.

Only the public key is stored in Paragon. The corresponding private key remains with the user and is used when connecting to the provisioned node.

The SSH Keys page displays the keys available within the current subscription. The page shows the key name, associated Resource Group, key fingerprint, and creation timestamp.

Manage SSH Keys

SSH Keys cannot be modified after they have been created. An existing key can be removed by selecting the required SSH Key and choosing Action > Delete.

Once deleted, the SSH Key is removed from the list of keys available for selection when provisioning new Compute Nodes.

Create an SSH Key

Click Create from the SSH Keys page to register a new SSH public key.

Enter a Name for the key, select the required Resource Group, and paste the SSH public key into the SSH Public Key field.

Click Submit to create the SSH Key.

Once successfully created, the SSH Key is displayed on the SSH Keys page and can be selected when provisioning a Compute Node.
a4594669-97dd-5f9e-a5fe-a1c5734f64bc.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > SSH Keys
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p164_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p165_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p165_2.png

21a69196-b344-5804-af5f-459a0e95bb3f.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Notifications
The Notifications page provides a consolidated view of platform-generated messages associated with activities and operations within Paragon. Notifications provide users with visibility into the outcome or progress of platform operations, including successful actions, failures, and informational updates.

The page displays the notification message, notification type, and the date and time at which the notification was sent.

The following notification types may be displayed:
21a69196-b344-5804-af5f-459a0e95bb3f.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Notifications

8a028bfe-cfc3-5c26-852e-3aeaa7b5fb7d.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Notifications
The following notification types may be displayed:
| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| SUCCESS | The associated operation or activity completed successfully. |
| FAILED | The associated operation or activity was unsuccessful. |
| INFO | Provides an informational or progress update for an operation or platform activity. |
8a028bfe-cfc3-5c26-852e-3aeaa7b5fb7d.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Notifications
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p166_1.png

f95b028d-6c11-5f0e-9153-1169e50b481b.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Notifications > View Notifications
Notifications are displayed with the most recent messages available from the Notifications page.

Use the Search field to locate notifications based on the required message or information.

The Notifications page is view-only. No additional actions or configuration are available for individual notifications.
f95b028d-6c11-5f0e-9153-1169e50b481b.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Notifications > View Notifications

80e2d16b-6d70-5e0b-b9f2-85a73ba3fe1a.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs
Transaction Logs provide a subscription-level record of operations performed within the Cloud Tenant Portal. They can be used to review activity across the subscription, identify whether an operation completed successfully, and investigate failed or in-progress transactions.

The Transaction Logs page displays the transaction description, Transaction ID, start and end times, status, user who initiated the operation, linked resources, and additional transaction details where available.

The following statuses may be displayed:
80e2d16b-6d70-5e0b-b9f2-85a73ba3fe1a.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs

34987ae2-3755-501c-aaca-c68a3b5ba3e4.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs
The following statuses may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Success | The transaction completed successfully. |
| Failed | The transaction did not complete successfully. |
| In Progress | The transaction is currently being processed. |
34987ae2-3755-501c-aaca-c68a3b5ba3e4.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p167_1.png

48b440a3-7b0c-575e-9bdd-08a108091972.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > View Transaction Logs
Use the Search field to locate transactions within the subscription. The Start Date & Time and End Date & Time fields can also be used to restrict the displayed transactions to a required time period.

Transaction Logs are maintained at the subscription level and therefore provide a consolidated view of operations performed against resources within the selected subscription.
48b440a3-7b0c-575e-9bdd-08a108091972.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > View Transaction Logs

f6e22fbe-ea59-537c-921b-5265688f161a.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > View Transaction Details
Click the Details (i) icon for a transaction to open the Transaction Details window.

The window provides additional information about the selected transaction, including the request description, transaction type, start and end times, user and organisation, creation and update timestamps, trace ID, subscription reference, and transaction status.

Where applicable, the Detail and Error Code fields provide additional information about the transaction outcome and can assist when investigating unsuccessful operations.
f6e22fbe-ea59-537c-921b-5265688f161a.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > View Transaction Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p168_1.png

2560a04b-92aa-5170-a5da-9a2b767757d4.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > View Linked Resources
Transactions that involve platform resources may display a Linked Resources icon. The number shown on the icon indicates the number of resources associated with the transaction.

Click the Linked Resources icon to view the resources associated with the selected transaction. The window displays the resource Type, UUID, and Name for each linked resource.

This allows the resources involved in an operation to be identified directly from the corresponding transaction record, including transactions that involve multiple related resources.

Transaction Logs are view-only. Resource management actions must be performed from the relevant resource section within the Cloud Tenant Portal.
2560a04b-92aa-5170-a5da-9a2b767757d4.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Services > Transaction Logs > View Linked Resources
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p169_1.png

d3dda864-8051-50d8-a7a5-495a66aad315.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration
The Administration section provides tools for organizing and managing resources within the current subscription. These functions support the administrative configuration of the tenant environment without directly changing the underlying operation of deployed workloads.

The available administration functions include Resource Groups and Instance Policies.

d8c2fccf-24d9-5c71-b997-80cc4d71d7e7.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Resource Groups
Resource Groups provide an optional way to organize related resources within a subscription. Resources can be assigned to a Resource Group to support logical grouping and easier management.

Resource Groups are an organizational construct and do not affect the operation or connectivity of the resources assigned to them.

The Resource Groups page displays the Resource Group name, the user who created the group, its creation time, and the user who last modified it.

Manage Resource Groups
Select a Resource Group to access the available options from the Action menu. Resource Groups can be renamed using the Edit option.

Edit a Resource Group
To change the name of a Resource Group, select the required Resource Group and choose Action > Edit.

Enter the new name and click Submit to save the change.

Create a Resource Group
Click Create from the Resource Groups page to create a new Resource Group.

Enter a name for the Resource Group and click Submit.

Once created, the Resource Group becomes available for selection when creating or configuring supported resources within the subscription.
d8c2fccf-24d9-5c71-b997-80cc4d71d7e7.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Resource Groups
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p170_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p171_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p171_2.png

bdcbc067-7b3f-57ef-b32f-00ecde31310e.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies
Instance Policies define the resource usage limits available to the current subscription for each infrastructure Provider. These limits control the maximum amount of compute, memory, storage, and Elastic IP resources that can be provisioned through the subscription.

The Instance Policies page provides a summary of the configured limits for each Provider. The page shows the maximum number of nodes, vCPUs, memory, storage, and Elastic IPs available under the corresponding policy.
bdcbc067-7b3f-57ef-b32f-00ecde31310e.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p172_1.png

5f98e7ab-984d-58a3-b8ab-c55f01032248.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies > View Instance Policy
Click the required Provider to open the Instance Policy details page.

The details page shows the current Threshold, Used, and Remaining capacity for each controlled resource, including Memory, Volume Storage, Virtual Machines, vCPU, and Elastic IPs.

This allows users to review both the overall resource limits assigned to the subscription and the remaining capacity available for provisioning.

The Request History section displays previous Instance Policy change requests for the selected Provider. Each entry shows the request ID, requester, submission and update timestamps, and the current request status.

Requests may be displayed as Approved or Rejected, depending on the outcome of the request.
5f98e7ab-984d-58a3-b8ab-c55f01032248.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies > View Instance Policy
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p173_1.png

75e6c3bb-4939-512a-af00-4ae56f5a30f7.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies > Request an Instance Policy Change
If additional resource capacity is required, click Request from the Instance Policy details page.

The Instance Policy Change Request page displays the current threshold, used capacity, and remaining capacity for each resource. Enter the required value under New Threshold for the resources that need to be changed.

Values that do not require modification can be left at their existing thresholds.

Review the requested thresholds and click Submit to send the change request.

The submitted request is sent to the Multi-Cloud Administrator (MCA) for review. The MCA can approve or reject the requested changes.

The outcome of the request can subsequently be viewed under Request History on the Instance Policy details page. Once a request is approved, the updated threshold is reflected in the Instance Policy.
75e6c3bb-4939-512a-af00-4ae56f5a30f7.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > Administration > Instance Policies > Request an Instance Policy Change
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p174_1.png

b86713ce-d334-5891-bcb5-76399184a867.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS
Bare Metal as a Service (BMaaS) enables physical servers to be allocated and managed directly from the Cloud Tenant Portal. Unlike Compute Nodes, BMaaS provides dedicated physical server resources based on the server sizes made available to the subscription.

The typical lifecycle of a BMaaS server is Allocate → Deploy OS → Use → Release OS → Deallocate. Allocation reserves a physical server for the subscription, while operating system deployment prepares the server for use.

After an operating system has been deployed, external connectivity is configured separately using Node Connect and the appropriate Network Policies.

The Servers page displays the servers currently allocated to the subscription, including the Server Name, Server Size, Region, Zone, Resource Group, current Status and Power Status, Subnet, and IP Address.

The following statuses may be displayed:

b04f72d1-53fa-5079-b6ad-7bc0f7ee0a17.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS
The following statuses may be displayed:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| Allocated | A physical server has been allocated to the subscription but an operating system has not yet been deployed. |
| Deployed | An operating system has been deployed and the server is available for use. |
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p175_1.png

1649cd31-2133-5d28-b50b-61feb84b281f.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Manage BMaaS Servers
Select a server to access the operations currently available for that server from the Action menu. The available actions depend on the server's current lifecycle state.

An Allocated server can have an operating system deployed or can be deallocated. Once an operating system has been deployed, it must first be released before the server can be deallocated.
1649cd31-2133-5d28-b50b-61feb84b281f.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Manage BMaaS Servers
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p176_1.png

8d361feb-75d5-52f3-950e-69b8ab90d49b.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Manage BMaaS Servers > View Server Details
Click the Server Name to open the Server Details page.

The page displays the server configuration and current state, including the Provider, Region, Zone, Resource Group, operating system, server status, Power Status, Subnet, IP Address, and hardware specification.

Additional information from the physical server is available through the Network Interfaces, Storage, Devices, and Security tabs. The Security tab includes information associated with server access, including the configured user and SSH key.

Available server operations are also displayed at the top of the Server Details page based on the server's current state.
8d361feb-75d5-52f3-950e-69b8ab90d49b.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Manage BMaaS Servers > View Server Details
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p176_2.png

e62f8f5f-b072-5b2e-bc0c-e911433e6801.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Allocate a Server
Click Allocate from the Servers page to allocate a physical server to the subscription.

Select the Provider, Region, Zone, and Resource Group, and enter a name for the server. Click Next to continue.

Select the required Server Size from the available options. Each Server Size represents a predefined physical server configuration and displays the associated CPU, RAM, storage, and GPU support.

The user selects the required Server Size rather than a specific physical server. Paragon allocates an available server matching the selected specification. A Server Size that is unavailable for allocation is displayed as a disabled option.

Review the selected server configuration and hardware specification. Click Submit to allocate the server.

Once allocation is complete, the server is displayed on the Servers page with an Allocated status. An operating system can then be deployed to prepare the server for use.
e62f8f5f-b072-5b2e-bc0c-e911433e6801.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Allocate a Server
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p177_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p177_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p178_1.png

8941f601-196b-5b77-bb1e-0fc09f69e36e.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Deallocate a Server
An Allocated server that is no longer required can be returned by selecting the server and choosing Action > Deallocate.

Deallocation is initiated directly and does not display an additional confirmation prompt.

A server with an operating system currently deployed cannot be deallocated. The operating system must first be released, returning the server to the Allocated state, before Deallocate becomes available.
8941f601-196b-5b77-bb1e-0fc09f69e36e.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Deallocate a Server

358f52e6-050d-596b-983b-35b47d038846.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Deploy an Operating System
An operating system can be deployed to a server once it has been successfully allocated. Select the Allocated server and choose Action > Deploy OS.

First, select an available Subnet for the server and click Next.

Select the required operating system from the available OS images. The available options display the operating system name, version, and distribution.

After selecting the operating system, provide the Host Name and Username to be configured on the server and select the required SSH Key. An existing SSH key can be selected, or a new key can be added using Create SSH Key.

These access settings are required as part of the operating system deployment regardless of the selected OS image.

Click Next and review the Server Information, Network Configuration, and Operating System Configuration. Click Submit to begin the operating system deployment.

Once deployment is complete, the server status changes from Allocated to Deployed. The server details page displays the deployed operating system, assigned Subnet and IP Address, and current Power Status.

To provide external access to the deployed server, configure Node Connect and the appropriate Network Policies as described in the respective sections of this guide.
358f52e6-050d-596b-983b-35b47d038846.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Deploy an Operating System
image_paths: documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p179_1.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p179_2.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p179_3.png
documents/page_images\Paragon User Guide - V2\Paragon User Guide - V2-p180_1.png

5ce0f419-0645-5d0c-a03f-c224023515ec.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Release an Operating System
When the deployed operating system is no longer required, it can be released from the BMaaS server.

Select the Deployed server and choose Action > Release OS. The option is also available from the Server Details page.

Review the server information displayed in the confirmation window and click Release to proceed.

Note: Releasing the operating system is a permanent operation.

Once the release operation is complete, the server returns to the Allocated state. A new operating system can subsequently be deployed to the server, or the server can be Deallocated if it is no longer required.

e00bea90-8806-556a-b432-929611eb30b2.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > BMaaS > Reset a Server After a Failed Operation
If an operating system deployment or release operation fails, the server may enter a Deployment Failed or Release Failed state.

When the affected server is opened from the Servers page, a Reset option becomes available on the Server Details page. Reset can be used to recover the server from the failed operation and return it to the Allocated state.

Click Reset and allow the recovery operation to complete. Once successfully reset, the server returns to the Allocated state and an operating system can be deployed again.

Note: Reset is a recovery operation intended for servers where the operating system deployment or release process has failed.

Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference
The following workflows provide a quick reference for common end-to-end operations in the Cloud Tenant Portal. Refer to the relevant sections of this guide for detailed configuration steps.
7abce5c0-e65a-5fd4-a0fc-3ccb74f309e4.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference

a4126840-be4c-5c4e-ae09-eec8d3e225c0.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Provision and Connect to a Compute Node
Create Node → Allocate Elastic IP → Create Node Connect → Create EIP Network Policy → Connect to Node

After the Compute Node has been created, allocate an Elastic IP in the same Zone and create a Node Connect to associate the Elastic IP with the node's network interface. Create an appropriate Network Policy to permit the required inbound traffic before connecting to the node.

To remove the resources, perform the operations in reverse order:

Remove Network Policy → Delete Node Connect → Release Elastic IP → Delete Node

Dependencies must be removed before their associated resources can be released or deleted.
a4126840-be4c-5c4e-ae09-eec8d3e225c0.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Provision and Connect to a Compute Node

fe5b6f36-124e-5382-af99-eed70c7c9a4f.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Provision and Connect to a Bare Metal Server
Allocate Server → Deploy OS → Allocate Elastic IP → Create Node Connect → Create EIP Network Policy → Connect to Server

Allocate a server using the required Server Size and deploy the operating system. Once deployment is complete, allocate an Elastic IP and create a Node Connect for the server. An appropriate Network Policy must then be configured to permit the required inbound traffic.

For teardown:

Remove Network Policy → Delete Node Connect → Release Elastic IP → Release OS → Deallocate Server

The operating system must be released before the Bare Metal server can be deallocated.
fe5b6f36-124e-5382-af99-eed70c7c9a4f.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Provision and Connect to a Bare Metal Server

d3436d90-f169-5b83-bab3-3bf869ff8c90.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Provide Outbound Connectivity through a NAT Gateway
Allocate Elastic IP → Create NAT Gateway for Subnet → Create Outbound Network Policy on Subnet

A NAT Gateway provides outbound connectivity for resources within its associated subnet. Each subnet can have one NAT Gateway. An appropriate outbound Network Policy must also be applied at the subnet level to permit the required traffic.

For teardown:

Remove Outbound Network Policy → Delete NAT Gateway → Release Elastic IP
d3436d90-f169-5b83-bab3-3bf869ff8c90.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Provide Outbound Connectivity through a NAT Gateway

90aac6e6-9b99-582c-9f86-09efa55426ca.text:
Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Enable Communication Between Two Subnets
Create Internal Route → Create Network Policy → Communicate Between Subnets

Creating an internal route establishes the route between the subnets but does not by itself permit network traffic. An appropriate Network Policy must also be configured to allow the required communication between resources on the two subnets.

For teardown:

Remove Network Policy → Delete Internal Route
90aac6e6-9b99-582c-9f86-09efa55426ca.section_path: Cloud Tenant Portal Administrator > CTP Quick Reference > Enable Communication Between Two Subnets
